title.rendered: How to fix the “Cannot Get Mail: The Connection to the Server Failed” error on iPhone

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Why the Mail app shows this connection error: Weak internet, wrong date and time, server outages, iOS bugs, or incorrect account settings often block your iPhone from fetching mail.
  • Check your internet before anything else: Confirm that Wi-Fi or cellular data is active and stable since the Mail app needs a reliable connection to load new messages.
  • Restart your iPhone to clear glitches: A quick reboot refreshes system processes, removes temporary mail sync issues, and often restores a clean connection to your email server.
  • Fix time-related authentication failures: Set your date and time automatically so secure mail servers can verify your device without running into avoidable connection errors.
  • Update password or re-add the account: Re-entering your email credentials or removing and adding the account again can fix authentication problems and restore proper server access.

Waiting for an important email and suddenly getting the “Cannot Get Mail: The Connection to the Server Failed” message is enough to ruin anyone’s mood. This message simply means your iPhone couldn’t connect to your email provider’s server and is almost always fixable with a few simple tweaks. 

In this guide, we’ll break down what causes this annoying issue and walk through 8 easy fixes to help your Mail app connect to the server and get emails again.

Why Your iPhone Says “Cannot Get Mail: The Connection to the Server Failed”

Before fixing the problem, it helps to know what’s causing it. Here are the most common culprits:

  • Weak or unstable internet connection: Your Mail app needs a solid Wi-Fi or cellular signal to fetch new messages. 
  • Wrong date or time settings: Incorrect time settings can break secure connections with your email server. 
  • Authentication issues: Recently changed passwords, expired login tokens, or missing account permissions can block server access. 
  • Misconfigured mail settings: Wrong incoming/outgoing server ports, disabled SSL, incorrect account type (IMAP/POP), or outdated settings often trigger this error. 
  • iOS bugs or outdated software: A glitch or an older iOS version can interfere with Mail app syncing. 
  • Server outage: Sometimes Apple, Gmail, Outlook, or your email provider is simply down. You may check it on the Apple System Status page.

Now that you know the probable culprits, let’s fix them.

8 Easy Ways to Fix “Cannot Get Mail” on iPhone

These steps resolve the error for most users. Start from the top and work your way down. 

1. Make Sure Your Internet Connection is Strong

Let’s start with the basics. The Mail app relies entirely on your network availability.  If your connection is weak, emails simply won’t load. So, first check your Wi-Fi connection.  

You can use an internet speed meter to measure your network speed. If it shows a slow connection, follow the steps below to boost the Wi-Fi signal:

  1. Go to Settings > Wi-Fi 
  2. Select your connected network, then tap Forget This Network > Forget.
  3. Reconnect to your Wi-Fi and test again. 

On the other hand, if you use cellular data, verify that the Mail app has access to it. 

  1. Open Settings and go to Cellular. 
  2. Scroll down and tap Show All.
  3. Here, ensure Mail is toggled on.
Quick Trick Toggle Airplane Mode on for 10 seconds, then turn it off. This refreshes your connection instantly.

2. Restart Your iPhone

A classic fix that still works wonders. Restarting your iPhone clears temporary glitches and helps the Mail app establish a stable connection with the email server.

  1. Hold the Side + Volume Up/Down button on your iPhone. 
  2. Drag the Slide to the power off slider.
  3. Wait a few seconds.

Press and hold the Side button again to turn your iPhone back on and check your inbox. 

3. Check Your Date & Time Settings

Incorrect time settings can break security certificates, blocking email sync. So, adjust the date and time to your location, ensuring the Mail app can retrieve new emails. 

  1. Go to Settings, select General, and tap on Date & Time.  
  2. Here, toggle on Set Automatically.
  3. Verify that the right Time Zone is displayed.

If not, turn off Set Automatically, tap Time Zone, and select the correct location.

4. Re-enter Your Email Password

If you’ve updated your email password on another device or your email address was signed out, your iPhone can’t authenticate. This can result in the “Cannot Get Mail: The Connection to the Server Failed” error. So, ensure that your mail credentials are up to date. 

  1. Open Settings, scroll down, tap on Apps, and select Mail.  
  2. Next, tap Mail Accounts and select the email address for which you’re getting the error.  
  3. You will see a Re-enter Password prompt at the top if there’s an issue with your account.
  4. Tap it and enter your updated login credentials.  

Once you’re done, toggle on Mail to sync your inbox for that account. On iOS, Gmail, Outlook, or Yahoo may redirect you to a re-authentication page. 

5. Delete and Re-add Your Email Account

If iOS doesn’t show a password prompt, your account configuration might be corrupted. Re-adding it resets all server configurations.  

First, you need to remove the email account from your iPhone with these steps: 

  1. Go to Settings > Apps > Mail > Mail Accounts.  
  2. Here, select the problematic email account and tap Delete Account at the bottom.  
  3. Confirm your choice by tapping Delete from My iPhone.

It will delete the inbox, your saved contacts, calendar events, and notes associated with this email from your iPhone. Don’t worry, your email stays on the server. Next, sign in to your email again.  

  1. Go back to the Mail Accounts page in Settings and tap on Add Account.  
  2. Type in your email address and tap Next at the top right corner. 
  3. If you’ve entered a third-party email provider like Gmail, tap Open Browser on the prompt, then enter your credentials.  
  4. Once added, toggle Mail on to loom yoemails on your iPhone.

After a few minutes, check your inbox to see if the error has been resolved.

6. Check Your Incoming & Outgoing Mail Settings

If you’re using a corporate account or a custom domain email address, manual configuration might be required. 

First, configure the outgoing server (SMTP): 

  1. Open the Mail Accounts settings and select the account that shows the error. 
  2. Tap Account Settings, select SMTP, and ensure it’s On 
     
  3. Finally, tap Gmail SMTP Server, then confirm that the Server Port is 465 or 587. 

Now, for the incoming server: 

  1. Open the Account Settings for the email address and tap Advanced. 
  2. Check if Use SSL is toggled on and if Server Port is set to 993 for IMAP and 995 for POP.

Not sure about these settings? Find them in Apple’s Mail Settings Lookup or contact your email host.

Pro Tip: To ensure your iPhone updates mail automatically, go to Settings > Apps > Mail > Mail Accounts > Fetch New Data. Here, toggle Push on and set Fetch to Hourly or higher.

7. Update to the Latest iOS Version 

Apple often releases bug fixes with the newest iOS release that can fix problems with mail syncing. To update your iPhone: 

  1. Go to Settings > General > Software Update.
  2. Tap Install Now if an update is available. 
  3. Now, wait for your iPhone to restart. 

Then, re-open the Mail app to see if new emails are loading again.

8. Reset all iPhone settings

If nothing has worked so far, some system-level config may be interfering. So, reset all settings to remove any conflicts preventing the Mail app from receiving emails.  

  1. Go to Settings > General, scroll down, and tap Transfer or Reset iPhone.  
  2. Here, select Reset, then Reset All Settings.  
  3. If prompted, enter your passcode, then tap Reset All Settings to confirm.
     

This resets Wi-Fi, VPN, network, keyboard, and system preferences to default. 

“Cannot Get Mail” Error Solved!

The “Cannot Get Mail: The Connection to the Server Failed” error is frustrating but usually easy to resolve. In most cases, the issue comes down to network hiccups, authentication problems, or misconfigured mail settings. Following the steps above should get your emails flowing again. 

If you still can’t receive Mail after trying everything, your email provider or Apple Support may need to check the issue on their end.

You may find these interesting:

  • How to fix the Mail app not working
  • How to change signature in Mail app
  • How to set up auto-reply in Apple Mail
  • How to clean Gmail using Manage Subscriptions

mainEntity.name: How long can the iPhone stay on StandBy?

acceptedAnswer.text: The StandBy mode, by default, turns off after a few seconds of no activity. However, if you own an iPhone with an Always-On display, you can customize the Standby mode to never turn the display off or off after 20 seconds.

mainEntity.name: Can I use StandBy mode without charging?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you can use StandBy mode without charging, as it is one of the primary requirements of the StandBy.

mainEntity.name: Why is StandBy Mode not working on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: There can be various reasons why StandBy Mode does not work on your iPhone, from charging issues to wrong iPhone placement to a software bug or glitch.

mainEntity.name: Does StandBy mode drain the battery on an iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: The StandBy mode does not drain your iPhone's battery. However, your iPhone might take a little longer to charge fully while in StandBy mode, as it also uses an undisclosed amount of energy.

keyPoints.title: Why Your iPhone Says "Cannot Get Mail: The Connection to the Server Failed"
keyPoints.explanation: This issue is usually caused by weak internet connections, incorrect date & time settings, authentication problems, misconfigured mail settings, iOS bugs, or server outages.

keyPoints.title: Check Your Internet Connection
keyPoints.explanation: Ensure your Wi-Fi or cellular data is strong and active, as the Mail app relies on a solid connection to fetch emails.

keyPoints.title: Restart Your iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: A simple restart can clear temporary glitches and help the Mail app reconnect to your email server effectively.

keyPoints.title: Verify Date & Time Settings
keyPoints.explanation: Correct date and time settings are crucial for secure server connections; set them automatically or manually adjust to your location.

keyPoints.title: Re-enter Your Email Password or Re-add Your Account
keyPoints.explanation: Updating your login credentials or deleting and re-adding the email account can resolve authentication or configuration issues.

title.rendered: How to Delete Workouts on Apple Watch the Right Way

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Why Apple Watch blocks direct deletion: Apple Watch doesn’t offer a delete option for workouts, so you remove entries from the Fitness or Health apps on your paired iPhone.
  • How to delete workouts on iPhone: You can open the Fitness app and swipe left on a workout to remove it or use the Health app to manage entries in bulk.
  • What Delete Workout vs Delete Workout and Data means: The first removes the logged workout, while the second clears all Apple Health metrics tied to that session and changes your Activity history.
  • How to fix accidental exercise minutes: You can search for the unwanted minutes in the Health app, swipe left on the entry, then delete it to correct your daily totals.
  • Precaution while editing workout history: Removing workouts or data in the Health app can’t be undone, so double-check entries before deleting to avoid losing accurate Apple Watch records.

Apple Watch remains one of the most reliable fitness tracking smartwatches. It captures your workouts with excellent accuracy and gives you a clear view of your daily and long-term fitness journey. Still, there are moments when you may want to delete a workout on Apple Watch, especially if you logged something by mistake, ended up with a duplicate entry, noticed incorrect tracking, or had your watch auto-detect an activity you never intended to record. The process is simple, yet many users aren’t sure where to look.

If you’re one of them, you’re in the right place. This post details how to delete, edit, and manage Apple Watch workouts so your fitness history stays accurate.

Table of Contents
  • Can You Delete Workouts Directly on Apple Watch?
  • 2 Ways to Delete an Apple Watch Workout
    • Using the Fitness App
    • Using the Health App
  • Delete Workout vs. Delete Workout and Data
  • How to Delete Accidental Exercise Minutes on Apple Watch
  • What Happens After You Delete a Workout?
  • Tips for Managing Workout Accuracy

Can You Delete Workouts Directly on Apple Watch?

No, you cannot delete a workout on the Apple Watch itself. Even though the Apple Watch records everything, stored workouts can only be managed in the Fitness app or the Health app on your paired iPhone. Once you delete a workout on your iPhone, the change updates across your devices.

2 Ways to Delete an Apple Watch Workout

The Fitness and Health apps store all your Apple Watch activity records, including every session you track. If you want to delete a workout on Apple Watch, this is where the actual cleanup happens.

Using the Fitness App

  1. Open the Fitness app and ensure you’re on the Summary tab.
  2. Now, tap the forward arrow icon in the Sessions tile.
  3. Here, you’ll see the list of all the workouts your Apple Watch has recorded so far.
  4. Next, find the workout you want to delete, and swipe left on it.
  5. Tap the Trash Bin (Delete) icon that appears.
  6. If you want to remove the workout but keep the calories and metrics, tap Delete Workout Only. If you want it removed completely, tap Delete Workout and Data.

Using the Health App

If your Fitness data is synced with the Health app, any workout shown in the Fitness app also appears in Health. You can delete it from here as well.

  1. Open the Health app and tap the Magnifying Glass (Search) icon at the bottom right corner.
  2. Search for Workouts and select it.
  3. Next, scroll down and tap Show All Data. You’ll see a list of all the workouts stored in the Health app.
  4. Swipe left on the workout you want to delete.
  5. Tap the Trash Bin (Delete) icon that appears.
  6. Finally, choose whether you want to:
    • Delete Workout Only
    • Delete Workout and Data

Delete Workout vs. Delete Workout and Data

When you delete a workout on Apple Watch from your iPhone, two options appear. They affect your Activity rings and Health data differently, so it helps to know what they mean.

  • Delete Workout Only keeps your calorie burn and exercise minutes, but removes the workout type. This is useful when the workout category was wrong, but the rest of the data is accurate.
  • Delete Workout and Data removes everything linked to that workout. Your calories, exercise minutes, and metrics will update instantly across Fitness and Health. Use this when the entire entry is incorrect or logged by mistake.

How to Delete Accidental Exercise Minutes on Apple Watch

Your Apple Watch sometimes awards exercise minutes even when you weren’t intentionally working out. A quick brisk walk, heavy lifting around the house, or a bit of energetic movement can trigger the sensors. Since this data often isn’t tied to a workout, you have to delete it separately.

  1. Open the Health app and tap the Magnifying Glass icon.
  2. Search for Exercise Minutes and select it.
  3. Scroll down and tap Show All Data.
  4. Now, swipe left on the data you want to delete.
  5. Tap the Trash Bin (Delete) icon that appears.

What Happens After You Delete a Workout?

After you delete a workout on Apple Watch through the Fitness or Health app, your Activity rings adjust to reflect the corrected calories. Your trends update and the workout disappear from your history. These changes help keep your progress accurate.

If a third-party app originally recorded the entry, it may reappear after syncing. In that case, open the third-party app and remove the workout there too.

Tips for Managing Workout Accuracy

While it’s easy to delete a workout on Apple Watch using your iPhone, preventing accidental logs saves time. You can make a few habits part of your routine, like checking the Workout app before moving, turning off Auto-Detect for activities you rarely use, locking the screen during water workouts, and ending workouts manually to avoid extra tracking.

Keep Your Workout History Clean

Knowing how to delete a workout on Apple Watch helps keep your fitness data reliable. Since all edits happen through the Fitness or Health app, you don’t need to handle anything on the watch’s small screen. It helps to check your logs regularly and remove accidental entries as soon as you spot them, so your Activity records always reflect your real progress.

If you’re stuck with an issue on your Apple Watch, feel free to ask in the comments, and we’ll guide you.

mainEntity.name: How long can the iPhone stay on StandBy?

acceptedAnswer.text: The StandBy mode, by default, turns off after a few seconds of no activity. However, if you own an iPhone with an Always-On display, you can customize the Standby mode to never turn the display off or off after 20 seconds.

mainEntity.name: Can I use StandBy mode without charging?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you can use StandBy mode without charging, as it is one of the primary requirements of the StandBy.

mainEntity.name: Why is StandBy Mode not working on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: There can be various reasons why StandBy Mode does not work on your iPhone, from charging issues to wrong iPhone placement to a software bug or glitch.

acceptedAnswer.text: The StandBy mode does not drain your iPhone's battery. However, your iPhone might take a little longer to charge fully while in StandBy mode, as it also uses an undisclosed amount of energy.

keyPoints.title: Apple Watch Workout Deletion Cannot Be Done Directly on Watch
keyPoints.explanation: Workouts on Apple Watch can only be deleted via the Fitness or Health apps on the paired iPhone, not directly on the watch itself.

keyPoints.title: Methods to Delete Apple Watch Workouts
keyPoints.explanation: Workouts can be deleted through the Fitness or Health app, either by swiping left on a workout and choosing to delete or by searching and managing workouts in the apps.

keyPoints.title: Difference Between Delete Workout and Delete Workout and Data
keyPoints.explanation: Deleting a workout only removes the category, while deleting workout and data removes all associated metrics, affecting your Activity and Health records.

keyPoints.title: Handling Accidental Exercise Minutes
keyPoints.explanation: You can delete unintended exercise minutes by searching in the Health app, then swiping left on the data and selecting delete.

keyPoints.title: Keeping Your Workout History Accurate
keyPoints.explanation: Regularly managing your workout logs by deleting incorrect entries helps ensure your fitness data remains reliable and reflective of your actual activity.

title.rendered: How to Find Lost Apple Pencil: 4 Simple Methods

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Why your Apple Pencil model matters: Tracking options differ across Apple Pencil Pro, USB C, 2nd Gen, and 1st Gen, so identifying your model helps narrow down the right method.
  • Find My works only with Apple Pencil Pro: The Pro model includes an Ultra Wideband chip that lets the Find My app guide you with precise distance and direction indicators.
  • Check Bluetooth for older Apple Pencil models: If you use the USB C, 2nd Gen, or 1st Gen Pencil, Bluetooth settings can confirm whether it’s nearby and still connected.
  • Use Bluetooth finder apps for signal clues: Apps like Wunderfind estimate distance by measuring signal strength, helping you locate a misplaced Pencil even when it isn’t actively paired.
  • Physical searching remains essential: Retrace your steps and check common hiding spots like sofa gaps, backpack pockets, or desk edges, using bright lighting to spot the Pencil’s slim white body.

Losing an Apple Pencil can be frustrating, especially when you’re ready to take notes or sketch and suddenly realize it’s missing. The good news is that, depending on the model you own, there are several ways to track it down. Even if your Apple Pencil doesn’t support advanced tracking, a few simple tricks can help you locate it quickly. 

This guide covers how to find your lost Apple Pencil or Pencil Pro, and offers smart habits to help you avoid misplacing it again.

Table of Contents
  • Which Apple Pencil Do You Have?
  • How to Find Your Lost Apple Pencil
    • Method 1: Use Find My to Locate Apple Pencil Pro
    • Method 2: Check Bluetooth Settings
    • Method 3: Use a Bluetooth Finder App to Track an Apple Pencil
    • Method 4: Retrace Your Steps and Nudge Things Around
  • Tips to Avoid Losing Your Apple Pencil Again
  • Get Back Your Lost Apple Pencil!

Which Apple Pencil Do You Have?

Before we jump into the search, let’s quickly figure out which Pencil you own. Because some support advanced Find My features, while others don’t.

How to Find Your Lost Apple Pencil

Here, I have shown 4 different methods based on the Apple Pencil model.

Method 1: Use Find My to Locate Apple Pencil Pro

If you have the Apple Pencil Pro, you’re in luck! It has an Ultra Wideband chip, so you can use Find My to locate it.

  1. Open the Find My app on your iPhone or iPad in portrait mode. 
  2. Move to the Devices tab at the bottom. 
  3. Tap your Apple Pencil Pro from the list. Here, you can see its last known location. 
  4. Tap Find to reach your Pencil. You will see a circle indicating its location.   
  5. As you move towards it, the text changes from “far,” to “near,” to “within reach.” 

Can’t see your Apple Pencil Pro on the list? Maybe you forgot to add it to your Find My. In such a case, follow the next method.

Method 2: Check Bluetooth Settings

To find the Apple Pencil Gen 1, 2, and USB-C models, you’ll need to use your iPad’s Bluetooth settings, as they don’t support Find My tracking.  

If it recently connected to your iPad: 

  1. Go to Settings → Bluetooth. 
  2. Ensure Bluetooth is toggled on.
  3. If your Apple Pencil is connected to your iPad, it is within 30 feet of your iPad.
  4. Walk around the area where you last used your Apple Pencil. If it disconnects, you passed it.
Pro Tip: If you see a low-battery alert on your iPad, it means your Apple Pencil is nearby. This alert only appears if your Pencil is still connected and within Bluetooth range.

Method 3: Use a Bluetooth Finder App to Track an Apple Pencil 

Checking Bluetooth connection status is a vague indication that your Apple Pencil is in close proximity. For a more granular search, use a Bluetooth tracker like the Wunderfind app. It shows the approximate distance between your iPad and Apple Pencil in meters.

  1. Download the Wunderfind app from the App Store. 
  2. Once the download is complete, launch the Wunderfind app. 
  3. Tap Allow when prompted to allow the app to use Bluetooth.
  4. If you want to use the app for free, just close the payment interface. 
  5. You can now view the accessories connected to your iPad. 
  6. Select the Apple Pencil from the menu, and a radar depicting the signal of the Apple Pencil will appear. 
  7. Move around until the signal strength reaches 100%. 
  8. When you find the Apple Pencil, tap I found it to conclude the search.

However, the app only works if your Apple Pencil has enough battery, is awake, and is connected to your iPad.

Note The Wunderfind app might take some time to accurately locate the devices. Please wait for some time so that the app loads the required data. However, please note that the app is not a hundred percent reliable.

Method 4: Retrace Your Steps and Nudge Things Around

If you still don’t have a location clue, this is your last resort. 

Think about the last time you used it. Was it on your desk, in a meeting, or at a coffee shop? Check common hiding spots, such as under furniture, in couch cushions, on desks, and inside bags and pockets. Use a flashlight to peer into dark areas. The Pencil’s white body can blend in, but it reflects light well. 

Also, move your belongings when searching. The pencil can sleep for a long time when disconnected, so it doesn’t appear on your Bluetooth list. Shuffling things can nudge the pencil to wake up and reconnect to your iPad if nearby.

Tips to Avoid Losing Your Apple Pencil Again 

Prevention is better than hunting, right? Here are some straightforward ways to keep your Pencil safe and sound. 

  • Use a magnetic iPad case with a pencil holder. This works especially well with Apple Pencil 1st Generation and USB-C devices, as they don’t attach magnetically. 
  • Add a silicone grip to your pencil. These holders keep it from rolling off desks and give it a personalized look. 
  • Regularly check the iPad battery widget to quickly notice when the Pencil isn’t connected. 
  • After every use, store your pencil in the same place, such as attached to your iPad, in a particular slot in your bag, or in a pencil case or sleeve. And stick to it. 
  • For non-Find-My models, attach an AirTag to it. It will help you track your pencil even if it’s discharged or out of Bluetooth range. 
  • Ensure that your Apple Pencil is charged after every use so you can use Bluetooth to locate it. 

Get Back Your Lost Apple Pencil! 

Finding a lost Apple Pencil can feel like hunting for a white needle in a white room. But with the right approach, like using Find My (for the Pro), Bluetooth clues, and smart search habits, you can usually track it down quickly. And once you do, a few simple preventive habits will help you avoid losing it again. 

Have you found your iPad buddy yet? Let me know in the comments below!

mainEntity.name: How long can the iPhone stay on StandBy?

acceptedAnswer.text: The StandBy mode, by default, turns off after a few seconds of no activity. However, if you own an iPhone with an Always-On display, you can customize the Standby mode to never turn the display off or off after 20 seconds.

mainEntity.name: Can I use StandBy mode without charging?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you can use StandBy mode without charging, as it is one of the primary requirements of the StandBy.

mainEntity.name: Why is StandBy Mode not working on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: There can be various reasons why StandBy Mode does not work on your iPhone, from charging issues to wrong iPhone placement to a software bug or glitch.

mainEntity.name: Does StandBy mode drain the battery on an iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: The StandBy mode does not drain your iPhone's battery. However, your iPhone might take a little longer to charge fully while in StandBy mode, as it also uses an undisclosed amount of energy.

keyPoints.title: Identify Your Apple Pencil Model
keyPoints.explanation: Knowing whether you have the 1st Gen, 2nd Gen, USB-C, or Pro model helps determine the best tracking method since features vary between models.

keyPoints.title: Use Find My for Apple Pencil Pro
keyPoints.explanation: If you own an Apple Pencil Pro, you can utilize the Find My app to locate it, thanks to its Ultra Wideband chip that allows precise tracking.

keyPoints.title: Check Bluetooth Settings for Non-eligible Models
keyPoints.explanation: For Apple Pencil 1st, 2nd Gen, and USB-C, checking Bluetooth connections on your iPad can help determine if the Pencil is nearby and connected.

keyPoints.title: Utilize Bluetooth Finder Apps
keyPoints.explanation: Apps like Wunderfind can help you track your Apple Pencil's approximate location by showing signal strength, making it easier to find even when it's out of Bluetooth range.

keyPoints.title: Retrace Your Steps and Search Common Hiding Spots
keyPoints.explanation: If digital methods fail, think back to where you last used the Pencil and physically search areas like under furniture, in bags, or pockets, using light to spot its white body.

title.rendered: Fresh Details Point to a More Flexible Future for the iPhone Air

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • iPhone Air not meant for yearly updates according to Bloomberg, countering reports of a delay due to low sales or hardware changes.
  • Second rear camera likely scrapped as Apple avoids a complex redesign for a feature rarely used in its target segment.
  • Next iPhone Air to debut 2nm A20 chip, bringing major efficiency and battery life improvements using TSMC’s next-gen N2 process.
  • Sales expected to remain modest, with internal estimates predicting just 6–8% of total iPhone sales, similar to the iPhone 16 Plus.
  • iPhone Air acts as a testbed for foldables, helping Apple trial future-facing tech like new materials and compact designs before wider rollout.

Apple’s roadmap for the successor to the iPhone Air is coming into sharper focus as recent reports shed light on what the device is set to offer and where it fits in the company’s longer-term strategies. Insights from The Information and Bloomberg indicate that the Air series is evolving into one of Apple’s most adaptable and ambitious iPhone projects.

Conflicting Reports About Delays

Earlier, The Information noted that Apple’s follow-up to the iPhone Air had been pushed back following slower than anticipated sales of the initial model, along with Apple’s interest in including a second rear camera. However, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman tells a contrasting story, stating that the device has been absent from Apple’s 2024 schedule for some time. This suggests that Apple may have never intended for the Air to receive yearly updates.

A Second Rear Camera Appears Unlikely

Gurman claims that the existing camera configuration is already too crowded to incorporate an additional lens without substantial redesign. Since the extra lens would likely be the least utilized across the iPhone lineup, the engineering effort seems misaligned with the Air’s relatively niche audience. A dual camera setup might only materialize if the design from Apple’s future foldable iPhones becomes widely adopted.

The Shift to a 2 Nanometer A20 Chip

The most significant change anticipated with the next iPhone Air is its internal shift. Gurman highlights that Apple’s focus is on migrating to a new 2 nanometer chip. This A20 processor, set to leverage TSMC’s N2 manufacturing method, promises noticeable gains in efficiency and battery life. For Apple, this silicon transition appears to be the keystone of the product’s development.

Modest Sales Expectations for the Air

Reports indicate that Apple internal assessments expect the iPhone Air to make up roughly six to eight percent of new iPhone sales. This mirrors the sales trajectory of the iPhone 16 Plus, positioning the Air as a selectively targeted device rather than a mainstream bestseller.

A New Release Schedule for 2026 and Beyond

Gurman presents a picture of Apple’s future iPhone release structure. By fall 2026, the company aims to unveil the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and its first foldable iPhone. Roughly six months later, Apple is likely to launch additional models, creating a cycle that could result in up to six new iPhones each year.

A Testing Ground for Apple’s Foldable Future

Beyond commercial strategy, the Air series serves an important internal purpose. Gurman suggests Apple uses the Air as a testing platform for materials, compact component designs, battery improvements, and software technologies that will be critical for the foldable iPhone. Many of these advancements are expected to debut with the Air before shaping Apple’s next major form factor.

What are your thoughts on the next iPhone Air? Share your opinions below.

mainEntity.name: How long can the iPhone stay on StandBy?

acceptedAnswer.text: The StandBy mode, by default, turns off after a few seconds of no activity. However, if you own an iPhone with an Always-On display, you can customize the Standby mode to never turn the display off or off after 20 seconds.

mainEntity.name: Can I use StandBy mode without charging?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you can use StandBy mode without charging, as it is one of the primary requirements of the StandBy.

mainEntity.name: Why is StandBy Mode not working on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: There can be various reasons why StandBy Mode does not work on your iPhone, from charging issues to wrong iPhone placement to a software bug or glitch.

mainEntity.name: Does StandBy mode drain the battery on an iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: The StandBy mode does not drain your iPhone's battery. However, your iPhone might take a little longer to charge fully while in StandBy mode, as it also uses an undisclosed amount of energy.

title.rendered: How to Fix iPhone Keyboard Lag

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Why iPhone keyboards lag: Low storage, outdated iOS, background apps, system bugs, or overloaded features like Predictive Text can cause slow and unresponsive typing.
  • Force restart to clear temporary glitches: Restarting your iPhone frees system memory, resets background processes, and often restores normal keyboard speed within seconds.
  • Update iOS and installed apps: Installing current iOS and app updates removes known bugs and improves overall typing performance across system keyboards.
  • Remove problematic third-party keyboards: Switching to Apple’s default keyboard eliminates conflicts from third-party apps that may slow typing or create delay.
  • Reset keyboard settings if issues persist: Resetting the Keyboard Dictionary and toggling features like Auto Correction or Predictive Text can fix mislearning and improve responsiveness.

There’s nothing more irritating than tapping away on your iPhone and watching the keyboard freeze, skip letters or lag behind your fingers. If your typing feels unresponsive or delayed, you don’t need to accept it as just how it is. Here are well-tested steps to fix iPhone keyboard lagging issues.  

Table of Contents
  • Why Your iPhone Keyboard Might Be Slowing Down
  • How to Fix Keyboard Lag on iPhone
    • 1. Force Restart Your iPhone
    • 2. Update iOS and Apps
    • 3. Remove Third-Party Keyboards
    • 4. Reset Keyboard Dictionary
    • 5. Disable Memory/Feature Intensive Keyboard Options
    • 6. Manage Background Activity & Storage
    • 7. Disable Predictive Text and Auto-Correction
    • 8. Enable “Reduce Motion”
    • 9. Toggle Keyboard Settings Off and On
    • 10. Test Across Multiple Apps
    • 11. Reset All Settings (Last Resort)
    • Contact Apple Support
  • iPhone Keyboard Lag, Solved!

Why Your iPhone Keyboard Might Be Slowing Down 

Before jumping into fixes, it’s helpful to know what often causes the keyboard to misbehave: 

  • Out-of-date iOS: Older or bug-ridden iOS builds can cause typing delays or glitches. 
  • Low storage: Having too many keyboards or languages installed can fill up storage, causing system responsiveness to suffer. 
  • Heavy memory usage: Running many apps or background processes can tie up RAM and slow down interactive features like the keyboard. 
  • Feature overload: Predictive text, autocorrect, haptics, and third-party keyboards each add processing overhead. 
  • System bugs: In iOS 26, users are reporting keyboard mis-mapping (pressing one key, getting another) and unresponsive keys, suggesting system-level issues.  
  • Third-party keyboard apps: They often have more features, but that can also create conflicts, especially on older iPhones. 

Knowing these helps decide whether a simple fix will do or whether more thorough troubleshooting is needed.

How to Fix Keyboard Lag on iPhone

Struggling with a slow or unresponsive keyboard on your iPhone? Try these simple fixes to get it working smoothly again.

1. Force Restart Your iPhone

A force restart clears temporary glitches and frees up system memory, making your keyboard function normally.

  1. Press and release the Volume Up button, then press and release the Volume Down button on your iPhone.
  2. Press and hold the Side button until the Apple logo appears.
  3. After restarting, see if typing is responsive. 

This will close all background apps and processes to reduce lag.

2. Update iOS and Apps 

If your keyboard lag is due to a bug, updating can solve it. 

  1. Open Settings and go to General → Software Update.
     
  2. If an update is available, download and install it. 

Also, update your apps via the App Store. Sometimes keyboard lag is isolated to a specific app due to compatibility issues. 

3. Remove Third-Party Keyboards

Third-party keyboards, such as Grammarly or SwiftKey, can sometimes slow down your iPhone. Try switching back to Apple’s default keyboard, which is lighter and more reliable.

To remove one:

  1. Go to Settings → General → Tap Keyboard.
  2. Select Keyboards at the top → Tap Edit at the top-right.
  3. Touch the red round icon to the left of the third-party keyboard.
  4. Finally, tap Delete to the right to remove the keyboard.

Keep the built-in keyboard and test typing again.

4. Reset Keyboard Dictionary

Corrupted custom word entries or keyboard settings can sometimes lead to weird behavior. 

To reset your iPhone Dictionary:

  1. Go to Settings → General.
  2. Tap Transfer or Reset iPhone, then tap Reset.
  3. Tap Reset Keyboard Dictionary.
  4. Enter your passcode when prompted.
  5. Finally, tap Reset Dictionary.

Keep in mind, this erases all custom words you’ve saved.

5. Manage Background Activity & Storage 

Running too many apps in the background can eat up RAM and cause lag. So, freeing up memory can restore responsiveness.

To stop background activity:

  1. Head to Settings → General → Go to Background App Refresh.
  2. Tap Background App Refresh.
  3.  Select Off to deactivate apps from running in the background.

Also, clean up unused apps, large files, and recently deleted folders. Ensure you have at least ~10–15% free storage as a general rule of thumb.

6. Disable Predictive Text and Auto-Correction

Predictive features can sometimes slow down typing.

Here’s how:

  1. Go to Settings → General → Keyboard.
  2. Scroll down and toggle off Predictive Text and Auto-Correction.

This also turns off Inline Predictions.

7. Enable “Reduce Motion” 

Animations and transitions can affect performance on older hardware.

  1. Go to Settings → Accessibility → Motion.
  2. Toggle on Reduce Motion.

This can make typing feel snappier by reducing UI load.

8. Toggle Keyboard Settings Off and On

Sometimes, a specific setting can cause your iPhone keyboard to lag. Try disabling all keyboard options (like auto-capitalization and spell check) if you’re unsure which one is the culprit. 

  1. Go to Settings → General → Keyboard. 
  2. Turn off all keyboard-related toggles (slide to type, spell check, smart punctuation, etc.). 
  3. Then toggle them on one at a time, testing typing after each change, until lag reappears.

9. Test Across Multiple Apps 

If lag occurs only in one app (for example, a heavy browser or social media app), it may be the app rather than the keyboard system.

  • Try typing in Notes, Messages, and Safari. 
  • If lag is confined to one app, update or reinstall that app rather than fix the system. 

10. Reset All Settings (Last Resort)

If nothing else works, resetting all settings resets system preferences without erasing your content. Back up your data first.

  1. Head to Settings → General → Transfer or Reset iPhone.
  2. Tap Reset.
  3. Tap Reset All Settings. Enter your passcode, then follow the on-screen instructions to restore your iPhone to its factory settings.
Note You will have to re-enter Wi-Fi passwords, reconfigure some preferences.

Contact Apple Support

If the problem continues, reach out to Apple Support. Since keyboard lag is usually software-related, they should be able to help quickly.

iPhone Keyboard Lag, Solved!

Your iPhone’s keyboard should feel responsive. If it doesn’t, you don’t have to live with a sluggish typing experience. Follow the steps above to quickly restore smooth performance. If you’re still having quirks, the issue may be systemic, so contact Apple Support for professional assistance. 

Did you get your keyboard working again? In the comments section, let me know what worked for you.

  • How to use Safety Check on iPhone

mainEntity.name: How long can the iPhone stay on StandBy?

acceptedAnswer.text: The StandBy mode, by default, turns off after a few seconds of no activity. However, if you own an iPhone with an Always-On display, you can customize the Standby mode to never turn the display off or off after 20 seconds.

mainEntity.name: Can I use StandBy mode without charging?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you can use StandBy mode without charging, as it is one of the primary requirements of the StandBy.

mainEntity.name: Why is StandBy Mode not working on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: There can be various reasons why StandBy Mode does not work on your iPhone, from charging issues to wrong iPhone placement to a software bug or glitch.

mainEntity.name: Does StandBy mode drain the battery on an iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: The StandBy mode does not drain your iPhone's battery. However, your iPhone might take a little longer to charge fully while in StandBy mode, as it also uses an undisclosed amount of energy.

mainEntity.name: Do AirTags interfere with credit cards?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. AirTags use Bluetooth and Ultra-Wideband signals that operate on completely different frequencies than credit card chips or their magnetic strips. Apple designed them to be safe next to cards. Just ensure the AirTag isn’t pressing too hard on the card’s surface to prevent physical wear.

keyPoints.title: Causes of iPhone Keyboard Lag
keyPoints.explanation: Outdated iOS, low storage, heavy multitasking, feature overload, system bugs, and third-party keyboards can all contribute to keyboard responsiveness issues.

keyPoints.title: Force Restart Your iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: A simple restart can clear temporary glitches and free up system memory, helping to resolve keyboard lag.

keyPoints.title: Update iOS and Apps
keyPoints.explanation: Installing the latest iOS updates and app versions can fix bugs that cause typing delays.

keyPoints.title: Remove Third-Party Keyboards
keyPoints.explanation: Switching back to the default keyboard removes potential conflicts from third-party keyboard apps that may slow down your device.

keyPoints.title: Reset Keyboard Dictionary and Settings
keyPoints.explanation: Resetting your keyboard dictionary and toggling keyboard features off and on can fix misbehavior and improve responsiveness.

title.rendered: Tesla Might Embrace CarPlay, Bloomberg Suggests

content.rendered:
According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman in his Power On newsletter, Tesla is expected to introduce Apple CarPlay support in the coming months. The report says Tesla will add the wireless version of CarPlay inside a dedicated window of its infotainment interface instead of replacing the full system.

This would be the biggest development for standard CarPlay in years. Tesla is the only major automaker that has continuously refused to adopt CarPlay despite high demand from customers. If the plan moves forward, it would mark a major shift for Tesla and for Elon Musk, who has repeatedly rejected the need for CarPlay in the past.

A Major Reversal After Years of Saying No to CarPlay

Tesla’s shift is surprising because the company has ignored one of the most requested features from buyers. CarPlay is offered in most modern cars and often influences purchase decisions, yet Tesla has always pushed its own interface as superior. Gurman calls the possible change a “stunning reversal.” The report notes that Musk could still change plans at any time, but Tesla appears to be preparing for a rollout.

CarPlay Will Run Inside Tesla’s UI, Not Replace It

Gurman says Tesla will not adopt the more advanced CarPlay Ultra system that takes over the entire display. Instead, regular wireless CarPlay will appear inside a section of the screen while Tesla’s native interface remains active. Navigation, vehicle controls, entertainment features, and other software will continue to function as usual.

Tesla already supports Apple Music and Apple Podcasts through its own apps. Adding CarPlay will allow drivers to access apps like Maps, Messages, and other third party apps without relying on the phone screen.

Why This Matters for iPhone Users and Future Tesla Buyers

If Tesla goes ahead with this update, iPhone users who depend on CarPlay will find Tesla vehicles more appealing. Many drivers avoid cars without CarPlay because they want consistent access to their apps, navigation, and messaging in any vehicle they drive.

Even though Tesla’s user interface is well regarded, CarPlay fills important gaps such as:
• Messaging with Siri
• Using preferred apps like Overcast or WhatsApp
• Keeping the same in car experience across multiple vehicles

The goal is not to replace Tesla’s infotainment system but to offer an additional option for drivers who want it.

Final Note

If Tesla does not pause or cancel plans, CarPlay support could arrive soon. For people who were waiting for this feature before purchasing a Tesla, the wait might finally be over.

mainEntity.name: How long can the iPhone stay on StandBy?

acceptedAnswer.text: The StandBy mode, by default, turns off after a few seconds of no activity. However, if you own an iPhone with an Always-On display, you can customize the Standby mode to never turn the display off or off after 20 seconds.

mainEntity.name: Can I use StandBy mode without charging?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you can use StandBy mode without charging, as it is one of the primary requirements of the StandBy.

mainEntity.name: Why is StandBy Mode not working on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: There can be various reasons why StandBy Mode does not work on your iPhone, from charging issues to wrong iPhone placement to a software bug or glitch.

mainEntity.name: Does StandBy mode drain the battery on an iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: The StandBy mode does not drain your iPhone's battery. However, your iPhone might take a little longer to charge fully while in StandBy mode, as it also uses an undisclosed amount of energy.

mainEntity.name: Do AirTags interfere with credit cards?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. AirTags use Bluetooth and Ultra-Wideband signals that operate on completely different frequencies than credit card chips or their magnetic strips. title.rendered: Tim Cook May Step Down as Apple CEO in 2026

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Tim Cook could leave Apple by 2026 as the board advances CEO succession plans after years of avoiding a formal timeline.
  • John Ternus is the leading successor with his oversight of iPhone, iPad, and Mac making him the top internal choice to replace Cook.
  • Apple leadership is being reshuffled following Jeff Williams’ exit, with key execs taking broader roles across Services, Software, and Hardware.
  • Cook’s tenure prioritized scaled production and global expansion, setting a stable foundation for a hardware-focused future under Ternus.
  • Transition plans are in motion, but not final and any leadership shift could significantly impact Apple’s product roadmap and innovation focus.

Tim Cook might be preparing to exit his role as Apple’s CEO as soon as 2026, according to a Financial Times report. The company’s board has begun laying out a succession plan, with internal leadership discussions reportedly moving into a more concrete phase. This marks the first time in several years that Apple has actively explored a leadership change timeline.

John Ternus as the Top Contender

John Ternus, Apple’s senior vice president of hardware engineering, is reportedly the leading candidate to replace Cook. Ternus oversees Apple’s full hardware product lineup, including the iPhone, Mac and iPad. If he takes over, he would become the first hardware-focused leader to run Apple since Steve Jobs.
Apple has a long history of promoting internal leaders. Tim Cook has previously stated that the company prefers internal continuity when selecting a CEO, making an external hire highly unlikely.

Cook’s Era and Apple’s Evolution

Cook, now 65, has served as Apple’s CEO for 14 years. During his leadership, Apple achieved massive product expansion and record financial growth while also facing controversies. One of Cook’s defining strategic decisions was scaling outsourced manufacturing, which allowed Apple to rapidly increase global production capacity.
The possible change in leadership comes immediately after another major shift. Jeff Williams, Apple’s longtime COO and previously viewed as a potential successor, retired recently. His departure triggered a wider rearrangement across executive responsibilities.

Expanded Roles for Apple’s Leadership

With Williams gone, various key executives have stepped into expanded positions:

  • Eddy Cue now oversees a broader range of Services
  • Craig Federighi plays a larger role in software engineering
  • John Ternus holds a more central leadership position on the hardware side

This restructuring suggests Apple is preparing for a future without Cook by distributing major duties across senior leadership rather than relying on a single replacement to inherit everything.

What the Transition Might Mean for Apple

If Cook steps down in 2026, it would be Apple’s largest leadership change since 2011. If Ternus becomes CEO, Apple is expected to continue prioritizing product development and could place even more long-term emphasis on hardware innovation.
Regardless of the exact timing, Apple appears committed to a smooth internal transition. Cook has previously said that Apple maintains detailed succession plans, and the recent leadership moves indicate those plans are now being put into action.

Leadership changes at Apple usually reshape the company and the industry. The next few months should provide clearer answers on where Apple is heading next.

mainEntity.name: How long can the iPhone stay on StandBy?

acceptedAnswer.text: The StandBy mode, by default, turns off after a few seconds of no activity. However, if you own an iPhone with an Always-On display, you can customize the Standby mode to never turn the display off or off after 20 seconds.

mainEntity.name: Can I use StandBy mode without charging?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you can use StandBy mode without charging, as it is one of the primary requirements of the StandBy.

mainEntity.name: Why is StandBy Mode not working on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: There can be various reasons why StandBy Mode does not work on your iPhone, from charging issues to wrong iPhone placement to a software bug or glitch.

mainEntity.name: Does StandBy mode drain the battery on an iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: The StandBy mode does not drain your iPhone's battery. However, your iPhone might take a little longer to charge fully while in StandBy mode, as it also uses an undisclosed amount of energy.

acceptedAnswer.text: There can be various reasons why StandBy Mode does not work on your iPhone, from charging issues to wrong iPhone placement to a software bug or glitch.

mainEntity.name: Does StandBy mode drain the battery on an iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: The StandBy mode does not drain your iPhone's battery. However, your iPhone might take a little longer to charge fully while in StandBy mode, as it also uses an undisclosed amount of energy.

mainEntity.name: Do AirTags interfere with credit cards?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. AirTags use Bluetooth and Ultra-Wideband signals that operate on completely different frequencies than credit card chips or their magnetic strips. Apple designed them to be safe next to cards. Just ensure the AirTag isn’t pressing too hard on the card’s surface to prevent physical wear.

title.rendered: Apple Hit With 634 Million Dollar Verdict in Apple Watch Patent Case

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple owes $634 million for patent violation after a U.S. jury ruled it used Masimo’s blood oxygen sensing tech without permission in Apple Watch.
  • Blood oxygen feature triggered a U.S. sales ban starting late 2023, which Apple bypassed by disabling the sensor via software in early 2024.
  • Apple’s 2025 fix shifts SpO2 processing to iPhone, letting watches show oxygen levels again without violating the hardware-based patent restriction.
  • Masimo is now fighting Apple’s workaround, with a new lawsuit targeting the iPhone-based approach to revive the blood oxygen feature.
  • Legal risks still hang over future Watch models as Apple appeals the fine and faces unresolved litigation that could block SpO2 features again.

A federal jury in the United States has ordered Apple to pay 634 million dollars to medical technology company Masimo for infringing a patent related to blood oxygen sensing in the Apple Watch. The report was first published by Reuters.

Why Apple Was Fined

Masimo accused Apple of using its patented blood oxygen monitoring technology without permission. The long-running lawsuit focused on how the Apple Watch measures and processes SpO2 data. Masimo called the verdict a major win for protecting its medical innovations. Apple responded by saying Masimo has sued it in multiple courts over 25 patents, most of which were found invalid. Apple also highlighted that the patent in this case expired in 2022 and covered older patient-monitoring technology.

Ban on Apple Watch Sales in the United States

The legal dispute affected Apple Watch sales in the U.S. starting in December 2023, when the blood oxygen feature caused an import and sales ban. Apple continued selling watches only during a brief interim appeal. When the ban was reinstated on January 18, 2024, Apple disabled the blood oxygen feature in software so the hardware no longer violated the ruling. This allowed the company to keep Apple Watch models available in the U.S.

Also Read: iOS 26 Beta 7 Brings Back Blood Oxygen Tracking to Apple Watch in the U.S.

Apple’s 2025 Workaround to Restore Blood Oxygen Monitoring

For more than 18 months, Apple Watch users in the U.S. could not use the blood oxygen feature. The capability returned in August 2025 through a redesigned system. Apple moved the processing of blood oxygen data from the watch to the paired iPhone. Users could still view SpO2 readings, but technically the watch itself no longer handled the measurement. U.S. Customs approved this workaround, allowing Apple to continue selling watches with blood oxygen support through the iPhone.

Masimo Is Still Challenging Apple

Masimo did not accept Apple’s workaround. The company filed another lawsuit aiming to overturn the U.S. Customs decision and stop sales of Apple Watch models that support blood oxygen monitoring in any form. A ruling on that new lawsuit has not yet been issued.

What Happens Next

Apple plans to appeal the 634 million dollar judgment. Until the appeal and the latest lawsuit are resolved, the future of blood oxygen monitoring on Apple Watch models in the U.S. remains uncertain.

mainEntity.name: How long can the iPhone stay on StandBy?

acceptedAnswer.text: The StandBy mode, by default, turns off after a few seconds of no activity. However, if you own an iPhone with an Always-On display, you can customize the Standby mode to never turn the display off or off after 20 seconds.

mainEntity.name: Can I use StandBy mode without charging?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you can use StandBy mode without charging, as it is one of the primary requirements of the StandBy.

mainEntity.name: Why is StandBy Mode not working on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: There can be various reasons why StandBy Mode does not work on your iPhone, from charging issues to wrong iPhone placement to a software bug or glitch.

mainEntity.name: Does StandBy mode drain the battery on an iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: The StandBy mode does not drain your iPhone's battery. However, your iPhone might take a little longer to charge fully while in StandBy mode, as it also uses an undisclosed amount of energy.

title.rendered: Apple Store App Gets Liquid Glass Overhaul and New Icon with iOS 26

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple Store app gets Liquid Glass redesign replacing the long-standing flat aesthetic with a translucent tab bar and updated textures.
  • New icon flips old color scheme with a white shopping bag on a blue background to match Apple’s updated visual identity across iOS 26.
  • No new features, only UI changes as version 6.6 focuses purely on design and performance without altering navigation or functionality.
  • Part of broader iOS 26 design rollout following similar updates to Apple TV and GarageBand, while iWork apps remain unchanged for now.
  • Visual overhaul may take months to complete with Apple apps updating first and third-party apps lagging behind; no user action required.

Apple has rolled out a major update to the Apple Store app following the release of iOS 26.2 beta 2. The app now adopts Apple’s new Liquid Glass design language, moving away from the long-standing flat aesthetic. This update was first reported by AppleInsider.

New Icon Embraces Liquid Glass Style

The most noticeable change is the redesigned app icon. Apple has inverted the earlier color palette. The shopping bag icon is now white and sits on a blue background. The look is consistent with the Liquid Glass visual style Apple showcased during WWDC and reflects the broader redesign taking place across iOS 26.

Complete UI Overhaul With Liquid Glass Tab Bar

The icon isn’t the only update. Inside the app, traditional buttons have been replaced by a Liquid Glass tab bar featuring translucent textures and subtle lighting transitions. The four navigation sections For You, Products, Go Further and Bag remain the same, so the update focuses purely on appearance rather than new functionality.

Expansion of Liquid Glass Across Apple Apps

This redesign is part of an ongoing visual refresh across Apple apps. The Apple TV app and its streaming platform received a similar Liquid Glass treatment earlier, including a real-glass redesign for the Apple TV logo. GarageBand has also adopted the new design style. In contrast, the iWork suite, including Pages, Numbers and Keynote, has not yet been updated.

Version 6.6 Includes Performance Improvements

Apple notes that version 6.6 also introduces various improvements and performance enhancements. There are no new user-facing features included in this release. The focus is entirely on bringing the Apple Store app in line with the new design language of iOS 26.

Major Design Shift Since the Flat Aesthetic of iOS 7

Liquid Glass represents Apple’s biggest visual change since the introduction of the flat UI style in iOS 7, which continued through iOS 18. It may take months for all optional Apple apps to receive this update and even longer for third-party developers to transition to the new interface style.

Apple’s steady rollout signals a clear goal to create a unified visual identity ahead of larger ecosystem changes expected with future software updates.

mainEntity.name: How long can the iPhone stay on StandBy?

acceptedAnswer.text: The StandBy mode, by default, turns off after a few seconds of no activity. However, if you own an iPhone with an Always-On display, you can customize the Standby mode to never turn the display off or off after 20 seconds.

mainEntity.name: Can I use StandBy mode without charging?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you can use StandBy mode without charging, as it is one of the primary requirements of the StandBy.

mainEntity.name: Why is StandBy Mode not working on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: There can be various reasons why StandBy Mode does not work on your iPhone, from charging issues to wrong iPhone placement to a software bug or glitch.

mainEntity.name: Does StandBy mode drain the battery on an iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: The StandBy mode does not drain your iPhone's battery. However, your iPhone might take a little longer to charge fully while in StandBy mode, as it also uses an undisclosed amount of energy.

title.rendered: How to Setup and Use Apple Passkeys for Secure Sign-ins

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • What Apple Passkeys replace: Passkeys let you sign in with Face ID, Touch ID, or a passcode instead of passwords, using FIDO security to prevent credential theft.
  • How passkeys protect your accounts: Each passkey pairs a public key on the service with a private key on your device, blocking phishing attempts and syncing securely through iCloud Keychain.
  • Requirements to use Apple Passkeys: You need iOS 26, iPadOS 26, or macOS Tahoe, plus iCloud Keychain and two-factor authentication, along with websites or apps that support passkeys.
  • How to create and use a passkey: Set up a passkey during account creation or conversion, then sign in by confirming with Face ID, Touch ID, or your device passcode.
  • Cross-platform use and management tips: You can use passkeys on Windows or Android through proximity verification, and manage or delete them anytime in the Passwords app on your iPhone.

Do you know that the strongest password can be stolen, guessed, or exposed in a data breach? That’s why Apple introduced Passkeys. It’s a more secure, password-free way to sign in to apps and websites using Face ID, Touch ID, or your device passcode. 

This guide breaks down what passkeys are, how they work, and how to set them up and use them across Apple and non-Apple devices in iOS 26, iPadOS 26, and macOS Tahoe.

Table of Contents
  • What Are Apple Passkeys?
    • Why Apple Passkeys Are More Secure Than Passwords
  • Requirements for Using Passkeys on Apple Devices
  • How to Create an Apple Passkey on iPhone, iPad, or Mac
    • Already have an account?
  • How to Sign In Using an Apple Passkey
  • Using Apple Passkeys on Non-Apple Devices
  • How to View, Manage, or Delete Passkeys on iPhone
  • The Security Behind Apple Passkeys
  • Recovering Your Passkeys if You Lose Your Device
  • Troubleshooting Common Passkey Issues
  • Passkeys Are the Future of Secure Logins!

What Are Apple Passkeys? 

Apple passkeys are a passwordless authentication method based on industry-standard FIDO technology. Instead of remembering and typing a password, you simply authenticate with Face ID, Touch ID, or your device passcode.

 

Each passkey consists of two parts: 

  • A public key, stored on the service you’re logging into 
  • A private key, stored securely on your device and never shared 

Apps or websites verify your identity by checking that your device possesses the private key. Since this key never leaves your device, it can’t be stolen through phishing or server breaches.

Why Apple Passkeys Are More Secure Than Passwords 

  • Phishing-proof: Passkeys only work with the real website they were created for. 
  • No passwords to manage: No resetting, forgetting, or reusing weak passwords. 
  • Safer during breaches: Servers store only a public key, not passwords that attackers can use. 
  • End-to-end encrypted syncing: Your passkeys sync across devices via iCloud Keychain. Even Apple can’t view them.

Requirements for Using Passkeys on Apple Devices 

Before using passkeys, ensure you have: 

  • An iPhone, iPad, or Mac running the latest versions (iOS 26 / iPadOS 26 / macOS Tahoe or later) 
  • iCloud Keychain enabled 
  • Two-factor authentication is turned on for your Apple ID 
  • A website or app that supports FIDO passkeys 
    (Examples: PayPal, eBay, Best Buy, GoDaddy, CardPointers, Dashlane, Nvidia, and major browsers like Safari and Chrome)

How to Create an Apple Passkey on iPhone, iPad, or Mac

Creating a Passkey happens when you sign up for a new account or update an existing one on a supported website or app on your Apple device. 

  1. Open the app or website and start the signup or login process. 
  2. When prompted, tap Continue with Passkey or Create Passkey. 
  3. Tap Continue and authenticate using Face ID, Touch ID, or your device passcode. The website will generate a unique key for your account. 
  4. The passkey is saved to iCloud Keychain and appears in the Passwords app.

If the option doesn’t show up, the site doesn’t support Passkeys yet. Also, you can have both a password and a Passkey for the same account.

Already have an account? 

No problem, most services now offer a Convert to Passkey option: 

  1. Sign in normally with your password. 
  2. Go to Account Settings > Security > Passkeys. 
  3. Select Create Passkey and authenticate. 
Tip On shared devices, choose Other options > Save on another device to store your passkey on a hardware security key instead of the device itself.

How to Sign In Using an Apple Passkey 

Once a passkey is created, logging in becomes instant: 

  1. Open the app or website. 
  2. Tap the username field. 
  3. Your saved passkey appears as a suggestion. 
  4. Authenticate with Face ID, Touch ID, or your device passcode.

No typing, no verification codes needed. Just authenticate and you’re in. 

Using Apple Passkeys on Non-Apple Devices 

You can sign in with your passkeys even on Windows, Android, or shared public devices. Your Apple device simply needs to be nearby, because the login uses secure proximity verification.

Here’s how it works: 

  1. On the non-Apple device, go to the website and enter your username on the sign-in screen. 
  2. For the Password section, choose Other Options, Passkey from nearby device, or a similar option. 
  3. A QR code appears on the device screen. 
  4. Scan the QR code using your iPhone or iPad.
  5. Approve the sign-in with Face ID, Touch ID, or your passcode.

Important: Screenshots or photos of the QR code won’t work. The process requires real-time proximity between devices. 

If you’re near someone else’s Apple device, you can also share a passkey via AirDrop.

How to View, Manage, or Delete Passkeys on iPhone 

All your Passkeys live in the Passwords app on your iPhone (it’s built-in on iOS 18 and later). Here’s how to handle them: 

  1. Open the Passwords app and authenticate yourself. 
  2. From the home page, tap the Passkeys tile. Here you will see all the accounts. 
  3. Select the account you want to manage. 
    • To change or update a Passkey: Just create a new one for that account following the creation steps.
    • To delete a Passkey: Tap Edit > Delete Passkey > Confirm. You can always create a new one later. 

From here, you can also share Passkeys securely with family groups. Everything syncs automatically to your iCloud Keychain, so changes appear on your other Apple devices, too.

The Security Behind Apple Passkeys 

Passkeys rely on WebAuthn, a modern authentication standard built on public-key cryptography. 

Here’s what makes them secure: 

  • Private keys stay on your device and never touch remote servers. 
  • Biometric authentication ensures only you can use the passkey. 
  • Phishing is impossible because your device checks the website’s real cryptographic signature. 
  • Server breaches don’t expose your credentials, since servers store only public keys—not passwords, hashes, or sensitive data. 

This model replaces the traditional shared-secret approach and eliminates attack vectors such as password reuse, credential stuffing, and SMS-based OTP hijacking.

Recovering Your Passkeys if You Lose Your Device 

If you lose one device, your passkeys remain available on your other Apple devices via iCloud Keychain. 

But if all your devices are lost:

You can still recover your passkeys using iCloud Keychain Escrow, a highly secure recovery system that protects your data even from Apple itself. 

You’ll need: 

  • Your Apple ID 
  • Your Apple ID password 
  • Access to your trusted phone number for SMS verification 
  • Your iCloud Security Code 
  • Your device passcode (once you set up a new Apple device) 

There are up to 10 attempts to recover your escrow records. Exceeding the limit deletes them permanently for your protection. 

You can also designate an Account Recovery Contact who can help you regain access if you’re locked out.

Troubleshooting Common Passkey Issues

Passkeys Are the Future of Secure Logins! 

Passkeys may sound technical, but in practice, they’re as simple as unlocking your device. They’re faster, safer, and more convenient than passwords, and they’re quickly becoming the new standard for secure sign-ins across the web. 

As more apps and services adopt passkeys, you’ll spend less time managing passwords and more time enjoying frictionless, secure access. 

What’s your experience with passkeys so far? Let me know below!

mainEntity.name: How long can the iPhone stay on StandBy?

acceptedAnswer.text: The StandBy mode, by default, turns off after a few seconds of no activity. However, if you own an iPhone with an Always-On display, you can customize the Standby mode to never turn the display off or off after 20 seconds.

mainEntity.name: Can I use StandBy mode without charging?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you can use StandBy mode without charging, as it is one of the primary requirements of the StandBy.

mainEntity.name: Why is StandBy Mode not working on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: There can be various reasons why StandBy Mode does not work on your iPhone, from charging issues to wrong iPhone placement to a software bug or glitch.

mainEntity.name: Does StandBy mode drain the battery on an iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: The StandBy mode does not drain your iPhone's battery. However, your iPhone might take a little longer to charge fully while in StandBy mode, as it also uses an undisclosed amount of energy.

acceptedAnswer.text: No. AirTags use Bluetooth and Ultra-Wideband signals that operate on completely different frequencies than credit card chips or their magnetic strips. Apple designed them to be safe next to cards. Just ensure the AirTag isn’t pressing too hard on the card’s surface to prevent physical wear.

keyPoints.title: Introduction to Apple Passkeys
keyPoints.explanation: Apple Passkeys are a more secure, password-free way to sign in using Face ID, Touch ID, or your device passcode, replacing traditional passwords with industry-standard FIDO technology.

keyPoints.title: How Passkeys Work and Their Security Benefits
keyPoints.explanation: Passkeys consist of a public key stored on the service and a private key on your device, making it phishing-proof, resistant to breaches, and syncing securely across devices via iCloud Keychain.

keyPoints.title: Requirements for Using Passkeys on Apple Devices
keyPoints.explanation: To use passkeys, you need a device running iOS 26/iPadOS 26/macOS Tahoe or later, iCloud Keychain enabled, two-factor authentication, and services supporting FIDO passkeys.

keyPoints.title: Creating and Using Passkeys
keyPoints.explanation: You can create a passkey when signing up or converting an existing account by authenticating with Face ID, Touch ID, or passcode, and then sign in seamlessly by using the saved passkey.

keyPoints.title: Using Passkeys on Non-Apple Devices and Managing Them**
keyPoints.explanation: Passkeys can be used on Windows, Android, or shared devices through proximity verification, and they are managed, viewed, or deleted in the Passwords app on your iPhone, with automatic sync via iCloud Keychain.
