title.rendered: Best GPS navigation apps for iPhone in 2026

content.rendered:
GPS navigation apps for iPhone and iPad have come a long way. They can help us search locations, turn-by-turn instructions, traffic navigation, and off-road directions. So, whether you’re hiking, traveling, or exploring your area, a map app is a must. Moreover, some GPS apps allow you to download maps to conserve mobile data and battery life. However, you must update your offline maps regularly to get accurate information.

We already have one GPS app for iPhone: Apple Maps. However, more choices are accessible, each with unique qualities. I have listed the best GPS navigation apps for iPhones below.

1. Apple Maps – Editor’s choice

Apple offers a pre-installed default GPS app for iPhone from iOS 6. So, it’s free and accessible to all. I liked its simple UI and turn-by-turn spoken instructions for bicycles, pedestrians, and vehicles. It gives an arrival time by calculating the current speed limit and real-time traffic data.

Besides, you may access real-time transportation information, including the bus or train’s arrival and departure schedules. Also, the interior airport terminal maps show the locations of eateries and bathrooms.

I got a Google Earth-like experience using its Flyover Mode and 3D city views. You may also communicate your ETA while biking, strolling, or using CarPlay with Siri to report a traffic incident while remaining hands-free.

Pros

  • 3D Look Around feature
  • Effective lane guidance and speed limit display
  • The navigation screen is free of distractions

Cons

  • Can’t download the map
  • Doesn’t warn drivers of speed traps or roadway obstructions.

Price: Free

Download

2. Google Maps – Best global GPS app

Google Maps offers a highly accurate points-of-interest database and map. Besides, with real-time traffic data and rerouting automation, you may quickly reach your destination and avoid traffic jams. The best part is it shows ongoing construction, accidents, potholes, and police presence.

You may view maps in different modes, such as traffic, public transportation, satellite, Google Earth, etc. I have made Google Maps default on my iPhone as I mostly use the Google Local Search feature to find new locations with their business hours, ratings and reviews, and other important information.

Additionally, it syncs your flagged location lists and search history across your logged-in devices. You may have voice instructions in regional languages, modify volume settings and play through Bluetooth.

Pros

  • Advance voice search
  • Accurate directions and location updates
  • Street views for 99% of U.S. public roads

Cons

  • Good for online usage
  • Offline maps take a large storage

Price: Free

Download

3. Waze – Best for drivers

Waze, an offering of Google, provides you the best navigation app for iPhone with the biggest community-based live traffic. In this app, the local drivers update real-time traffic and route information from time to time.

So, plan your journey accordingly with dynamic routing and save time. Besides, you can find the cheapest petrol along your route to save money. But you must have the internet to access the live map and interact with other drivers.

You may also give updates about construction, road hazards, speed traps, etc., by connecting Waze with FourSquare, Twitter, or Facebook. I loved its compatibility with playing music and podcasts directly from the app. You can also use it on your car’s display while driving with Apple CarPlay.

Pros

  • Real-time traffic information
  • Apple CarPlay compatibility
  • Rerouting automation
  • Driver’s community

Cons

  • Ads on the screen
  • Little point-of-interest location information

Price: Free

Download

You must read: Waze vs Google Maps: Which is the better navigation app?

4. Citymapper – Best for transportation

CityMapper allows planning your journey in the shortest time by comparing transportation alternatives. So, whatever transit mode you choose, including walking, biking, or public transit, you can easily traverse using turn-by-turn instructions.

Besides, the app offers three different map views, official offline maps, and no-parking zone alerts. Therefore, this app is your travel companion if you live in NYC or the San Francisco Bay Area. Also, you may compare taxi prices, book a rental car, or locate an e-scooter nearby, thanks to its integration with the bike and car rental apps.

I always plan my journey according to its real-time wait times and ETAs to avoid missing buses or trains during rush hour. Besides, track your bus or train, check the best train car to board, and choose the right entrance and exit at every subway or railway station.

Pros

  • Aggregates all transit systems
  • Compatible with Apple Watch
  • Share your live ETA and location via iMessages

Cons

  • Crashes on older iPhones
  • Drains battery too fast

Price: Free (In-app purchases start from $1.49)

Download

5. Avenza – Best offline GPS app

Avenza is my favorite app for offline maps, perfect for preplanning an adventure or hiking trip. It offers a large offline map store, including National Geographic maps, national park maps, etc. Also, you may access premium maps of Garmin, USGS, Michelin, etc.

The “trace your steps” feature tracks you down anywhere globally. Besides, you can create geofences worldwide. I liked its integration with what3words to pinpoint your position with custom symbol sets and alternative coordinate display formats.

Also, you can import unlimited geographic PDF, GeoPDF, and GeoTIFF maps and attach notes, images, and CSV, GPX, and KML files. So, whether riding off-roads or hiking remote trails, Avenza is there for you.

Pros

  • The world’s largest map collection for downloading
  • Record GPS tracks and mark spots
  • Import your own maps

Cons

  • The tracking feature obstructs the view of that map
  • The interface is not user-friendly

Price: Free (In-app purchases start from $0.99)

Download

6. MapQuest – For night-mode lovers

MapQuest provides every essential feature you need to explore and travel the United States and Canada. You may use voice navigation for walking or driving instructions or explore areas of interest on the map. Besides, it supports Apple CarPlay and a live traffic camera.

Also, you can view live satellite images and real-time traffic updates to avoid traffic and take alternative routes. I liked its built-in speedometer that compares your current speed to the posted speed limits on your road. Besides, the multipoint itineraries feature allows you to set more than one-stop trips.

You can also use custom symbols to designate preferred destinations. While planning, I use its layers bar to find and explore surrounding attractions like restaurants, petrol stations with the lowest costs, etc. Besides, it’s one of the GPS navigation apps for iPhone that lets you discover fantastic hotel offers and reserve them within the app.

Also, you can look at menus, book reservations, and place food orders through OpenTable and GrubHub. I think its most unique feature is local weather updates. But the pop-up ads are frustrating and obstruct the map view.

Pros

  • Get live traffic updates and alternate route options
  • Speed limit display
  • App shortcuts

Cons

  • Doesn’t work properly with Siri
  • The navigational capabilities are inoperable in offline mode

Price: Free

Download

7. Sygic – Get 3D downloadable maps

The most sophisticated iPhone GPS app with a great navigation experience, smart tools, stunning 3D downloadable maps, and an intuitive user interface. The GPS multi-lingual voice guidance provides clear instructions and speaks street names.

Also, offline maps get free updates regularly. If you love exploring cities on foot, this app is for you. Because it covers every point-of-interest location and tourist site with walking instructions. Also, you can customize your navigation arrow.

Over 500 million people globally provide real-time traffic information, and Dynamic Lane Assistant helps to avoid traffic congestion. Besides, Speed restriction alerts display the current speed limit. Also, the Sygic app emphasizes your safety. 

The Real View Navigation and Head-up Display technology is helpful in nighttime driving as it projects navigation onto the windshield. After a collision, a dashcam instantly captures a video of the surrounding area.

Besides, Apple CarPlay connectivity displays all navigational tools on the in-dash display. I liked its wrong-way alert (developed in collaboration with Bosch) to know if you’re going the incorrect way.

Pros

  • Head-up display
  • Real-time sign detection
  • Support for Dashcam and Cockpit
  • Dynamic Lane Assistant

Cons

  • Costly subscription
  • Unstable with CarPlay

Price: Free (In-app purchases start from $12.49)

Download

8. MAPS.ME – Find the best hotel

If you are looking for an offline GPS app that drains your battery, MAPS.ME is the one. With its ready-made travel guides, you save time arranging the trip and ensure you never miss a location or outdoor activities.

Besides, the app offers detailed directions to hiking paths, POIs, and other offbeat locations, indicating whether a route is uphill or downhill. Also, millions of OpenStreetMap contributors update maps every day. 

It shows hiking trails and other features with MAPS.ME’s extensive tourist spots database. Along with using optimized navigation, you can do offline searches and browse several categories, such as eateries, tourist destinations, hotels, ATMs, and public transportation.

Besides, directly reserve hotels on Booking.com using the app. So, give MAPS. Give me a try, as every single free map and little advertisement is available in the app.

Pros

  • Get the most optimal route
  • Search location by category
  • Bookmark favorite spots

Cons

  • Poor navigation in rural areas
  • Doesn’t choose the shortest route

Price: Free (In-app purchases start from $0.99)

Download

9. TomTom Go – Drive to your photo

TomTom GO lets you enjoy downloadable 3D offline maps updated weekly with accurate real-time traffic. Also, the dynamic lane assistance and simple turn-by-turn guidance let you reach your location quickly.

The speed alerts warn for stationary and moving speed cameras. With Apple CarPlay, enjoy best-in-class navigation on display in your vehicle. Besides, I liked its ads-free interface, which is more effective and privacy-focused.

Another unique feature called “Drive to a Photo” gives directions to the locations of your geotagged pictures and the addresses of the contacts on your phone. Along with offline maps, you may search online to find destinations, well-known sights, and crucial POIs.

You can discover alternative routes to avoid traffic jams using the TomTom Traffic function’s accurate distance and timing estimates. Besides, you can share your arrival time with others using the messaging service.

But the biggest turnoff for me is you only receive 50 miles of free navigation each month. If you want more, you will need to subscribe.

Pros

  • 150+ countries’ downloadable 3D maps with weekly updates
  • Speed camera alerts
  • Directions for geotagged photos

Cons

  • The free app includes 50 miles of navigation per month
  • The iPhone route bar isn’t available on CarPlay

Price: Free (In-app purchases start from $4.99)

Download

10. MapFactor – Free offline maps

Mapsfactor is one of the best free GPS navigation apps for iPhone from OpenStreetMaps. It offers free offline maps of more than 200 countries with monthly map updates.

You will get HD live traffic, a door-to-door route, and a summary of the planned trip. Besides, the speed restrictions and camera alerts keep you safe. You can set the intuitive voice turn-by-turn directions in your preferred language. 

The app’s premium offers professional TomTom navigation maps with UK postcodes for more dependable and accurate driving. Also, I liked its day and night map modes with 2D/3D settings to navigate realistic visual maps.

You may modify your vehicle details to improve diverse routes. Besides, the Heads-Up Display feature and support for CarPlay enhance your night drive.

Pros

  • Free maps of more than 200 countries
  • Customize your vehicle details for accurate routing
  • Head-up display for night drives

Cons

  • Poor searching
  • UI is backdated

Price: Free (In-app purchases from $1.99)

Download

So, that’s all for today, folks!

You should get your iPhone’s best GPS navigation app if you commute daily or love exploring new locations. The offline GPS app has the advantage that it doesn’t drain the battery of your iPhone or produce heat. So, which app are you going to download? Let me know in the comment section!

title.rendered: How to Use Visual Intelligence on iPhone to Translate, Search, and Ask ChatGPT

content.rendered:
Apple first introduced Visual Intelligence with iOS 18.2, a feature that could recognize what your iPhone’s camera saw in real time. With iOS 26, Apple takes it a step further. Visual Intelligence can now analyze both what’s in front of your camera and anything displayed on your screen. That means you can identify objects, translate text, shop online, or even ask ChatGPT questions about what you see.

Here’s a full guide on how to use Visual Intelligence on your iPhone.

Table of Contents
  • What is Visual Intelligence?
  • Which iPhones Support Visual Intelligence?
  • How to Use Visual Intelligence on iPhone
    • 1. Get Information About Places and Businesses
    • 2. Interact with Text in Real Time
    • 3. Ask ChatGPT for More Information
    • 4. Search for Related Images on Google
    • 5. Add Events to Calendar from Posters or Flyers
    • 6. Instantly Identify a Plant or Animal
  • How to Use Visual Intelligence via the Action Button
    • To set it up:
    • Use Visual Intelligence via Action Button
  • What's New with Visual Intelligence in iOS 26
  • Unlock the Full Potential of Visual Intelligence

What is Visual Intelligence?

Visual Intelligence is an Apple Intelligence-powered feature that combines on-device AI with real-time visual understanding. It debuted with the iPhone 16 series and requires at least an A17 Pro chip with an advanced Neural Engine for fast, private processing.

With it, your iPhone can recognize and extract details from what your camera or screen shows, from identifying a plant to translating a menu, finding products online, or getting instant help from ChatGPT.

Which iPhones Support Visual Intelligence?

Visual Intelligence is part of Apple Intelligence, available on the following models:

iPhone 15 Pro, 15 Pro Max, iPhone 16, 16 Plus, 16e, 16 Pro, 16 Pro Max, iPhone 17, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max, and iPhone Air.

How to Use Visual Intelligence on iPhone

From learning about nearby businesses to translating text or chatting with ChatGPT, Visual Intelligence can be your everyday AI assistant. Here’s how to use it.

1. Get Information About Places and Businesses

Visual Intelligence can show you business hours, menus, and contact details just by pointing your camera.

  1. Point your iPhone camera toward the business and long press the Camera Control to invoke Visual Intelligence.
  2. Press the Camera Control again or tap the capture button on the display to analyze the business.
  3. Now, based on the business type, Visual Intelligence will suggest actions including but not limited to:
    • View Schedule: To reveal the operational hours
    • Order: For placing an order with the business
    • Menu: To view the business’s menu or services

Besides these actions, you’ll also find options to call the business, view its website, and more.

Note This feature is currently available only in the U.S.

2. Interact with Text in Real Time

Visual Intelligence brings Live Text to a new level. Aim your camera at any printed or on-screen text, and your iPhone can instantly summarize, translate, or act on it.

  1. Point the camera toward the text and long-press the Camera Control to bring up Visual Intelligence.
  2. Press the Camera Control again or tap the capture button on the display to analyze the text.
  3. Depending on the text, Visual Intelligence will suggest actions such as summarizing, translating, reading aloud, visiting the website, calling the phone number, and more. Tap the one you prefer.
    • For example, I used Visual Intelligence to summarize the text in the image below.

3. Ask ChatGPT for More Information

Apple’s ChatGPT integration in iOS 18 makes Visual Intelligence even smarter. You can ask detailed follow-up questions about anything your camera sees.

  1. Frame the subject in your iPhone’s Camera app and tap the Ask button at the bottom.
  2. Grant ChatGPT the necessary permissions when prompted and tap Enable ChatGPT. You can choose to use ChatGPT with an account if you want. (You only need to do this the first time you use the ChatGPT integration with Visual Intelligence.)

  3. Give it a few seconds, and you’ll see the result for your search in a ChatGPT card at the top of the screen. You can also type or dictate a follow-up question in the text field below if you need further information.
  4. Tap the X button in the bottom-right corner to exit Visual Intelligence.

4. Search for Related Images on Google

Want to find similar items online? Visual Intelligence can reverse-image search using Google.

  1. Direct your iPhone’s camera toward the object and long-press the Camera Control to access Visual Intelligence.
  2. Tap the Search button in the bottom-right corner, and a Searching with Google dialog box will appear, followed by the search results.

5. Add Events to Calendar from Posters or Flyers

Starting with iOS 18.3, Visual Intelligence can detect event details from posters or flyers and help you add them to your Calendar.

How to do it:

  1. Press & hold the Camera Control button to open Visual Intelligence.
  2. Position the iPhone cameras on a flyer or poster with a date.
  3. A Create Event button will appear at the top center; tap on it to let Visual Intelligence identify the event.
  4. Once identified, Visual Intelligence will prompt you to schedule the event; tap the Schedule button to complete calendar event creation.

6. Instantly Identify a Plant or Animal

With iOS 18.3 or later, identifying flora and fauna is effortless.

  1. Open Visual Intelligence and position the iPhone camera towards the subject (plant or animal) you want to identify.
  2. Visual Intelligence will automatically identify the subject and display its name at the top center.
  3. Tap on the subject’s name to get more information.

Note Visual Intelligence may show “May Be” if it’s unsure.

How to Use Visual Intelligence via the Action Button

If your iPhone doesn’t have a Camera Control button, you can still access Visual Intelligence using the Action Button.

To set it up:

  1. Open Settings and head to the Action Button settings.
  2. Here, swipe right or left until the Visual Intelligence appears.

Use Visual Intelligence via Action Button

Once configured, long-press the Action Button to invoke Visual Intelligence and start using it just like on the iPhone 16 and 17 series.

What’s New with Visual Intelligence in iOS 26

iOS 26 introduces a major upgrade. Visual Intelligence now works with screenshots. You can circle any part of a screenshot to search or ask ChatGPT instantly.

  1. Take a screenshot by pressing the Side button + Volume button.
  2. Now, use your finger to circle the part of the image you’re interested in. A new Siri-style glow animation will appear around the circled part.  
  3. Tap the Ask button and type a question, or tap the Image Search button or swipe up to reverse image search on the internet.

Use this to compare prices, research images, or get more context about what’s on your screen.

Unlock the Full Potential of Visual Intelligence

Visual Intelligence redefines how your iPhone sees and understands the world. Whether you’re identifying a plant, translating signs, or using ChatGPT for instant answers, it’s a powerful new way to connect the physical and digital worlds.

Are you using Visual Intelligence on your iPhone 17? Share your favorite feature in the comments below. We’d love to hear how you’re using it.

Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: iPhone 18 Pro to Feature Smaller Display Hole and Under-Display Face ID

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • iPhone 18 Pro may shrink the Dynamic Island using HIAA laser-drilling tech, reducing the camera hole for a cleaner OLED display.
  • Under-display Face ID is being tested to further minimize screen cutouts, aiming for a near full-screen iPhone experience.
  • iPhone 18 Pro Max might get a transparent back and steel-shell battery, hinting at vapor chamber cooling and a Nothing Phone-style aesthetic.
  • Camera upgrades include a variable aperture lens on the main rear sensor, improving low-light shots without changing the signature camera bump.
  • Staggered launch expected from 2026 with Pro and Air models in September, followed by iPhone 18 and 18e in spring 2027.

Apple might be heading toward a sleek new display change for its next iPhone Pro models. A Chinese leaker known as Digital Chat Station has hinted on Weibo that the tech giant is possibly working on a way to shrink the front-facing camera for the anticipated iPhone 18 Pro series.

Apple Testing HIAA Technology for a Smaller Camera Hole

The leaker suggests Apple is looking into a novel method called HIAA (Hole-In-Active-Area) technology. Developed by Samsung and others in the display game, this technique could help blend the camera seamlessly into the OLED screen, reducing visual clutter on the screen. Essentially, this involves precise laser micro-drilling to create a tiny opening right within the display itself, allowing the camera to take up less space compared to the current Dynamic Island.

Earlier this year, Digital Chat Station also pointed out that Apple might couple this development with under-display Face ID. If these claims hold water, it would mean a more uninterrupted iPhone display, save for a small camera hole peeking through.

Smaller Dynamic Island and Design Changes Expected

With this HIAA technology, the screen’s shape might see some tweaks—perhaps a nod to subtle shifts in the display’s curvature. While the exact positioning of the front camera remains a mystery, whispers in the tech community suggest that the Dynamic Island could just become smaller, making for a less intrusive interface while keeping it in place.

When it comes to the rest of the design, the iPhone’s rear is expected to stick with its familiar look. Reports suggest the iPhone 18 Pro will retain the plateau-style camera design seen in its predecessor, the iPhone 17 Pro. On the flip side, Apple might spice things up with an upgraded main camera sporting a more advanced variable aperture lens to enhance shots in different lighting.

Transparent Back and Steel-Shell Battery for Pro Max Model

In an unexpected twist, there are rumors that the iPhone 18 Pro Max might showcase a transparent section on its back, offering a peek at its inner workings—a move reminiscent of the approach used by Nothing phones. Additionally, there’s talk of Apple testing a steel-shell battery. This likely points to a stainless steel vapor chamber cooling system, which could promise better heat management during use.

Expected Launch Timeline

According to the report, Apple appears to be gearing up for a September 2026 launch of the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and a new model dubbed the iPhone Air. Following after, the standard iPhone 18 and the iPhone 18e might debut in spring 2027, part of what might be a strategic shift to a staggered release cycle.

These insights originate from Digital Chat Station on Weibo, with supporting info from The Information and supply chain reports tied to display technology developments.

What do you think about these potential changes? Share your thoughts below.

title.rendered: iPhone Fold to Feature Industry First 24MP Under-Display Camera

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple’s foldable iPhone may debut a 24MP under-display camera, solving clarity issues that plague current 4–8MP solutions from Samsung and ZTE.
  • Six-element lens boosts light capture, letting Apple deliver sharper, more usable selfies even through the screen—an industry first if accurate.
  • No Face ID, LiDAR, or OIS on foldable model to preserve compact design; includes dual 48MP rear cameras and Touch ID on the side.
  • All iPhone 18 flagships to feature 24MP front cameras, improving portrait mode, edge detection, and skin tone rendering across the board.
  • Launch expected in fall 2026 or spring 2027, as Apple fine-tunes hinge design and shifts to staggered flagship vs standard iPhone releases.

Apple’s upcoming foray into foldable phones might break new ground with a 24-megapixel under-display camera, according to an equity research report by JP Morgan, shared by MacRumors. This would be a notable advancement in under-display technology, which until now, has struggled to offer high-quality images.

Apple Reportedly Surpasses Under-Display Challenges

While under-display cameras have appeared in several Android models like the ZTE Axon 40 Ultra and Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold series, they often feature lower-resolution sensors, typically around 4MP or 8MP. This is due to the difficulty in maintaining image clarity through the layers of the screen. Apple’s choice of a 24MP sensor, enhanced by six plastic lens elements, is said to improve light transmission, producing sharper and more detailed images. Should this be accurate, Apple could be the first to deliver a genuinely practical under-display camera for everyday use.

Compact Design May Lead to Some Omissions

However, the JP Morgan report also highlights that Apple has made design trade-offs to keep its foldable iPhone sleek and compact. Notably, it might omit LiDAR and optical image stabilization, features standard in current iPhone Pro models. Nevertheless, the foldable model is expected to include a dual 48MP rear camera setup along with two front-facing cameras: a visible one on the outer screen (punch-hole) and an under-display one on the inner screen.

For biometric authentication, Touch ID is anticipated to be built into the side button, as Apple opts out of using Face ID this time, likely to conserve space.

Part of a Wider 24MP Camera Upgrade Across iPhone 18 Lineup

The report from JP Morgan also suggests that all the flagship devices in the upcoming iPhone 18 lineup, including the iPhone 18, 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max, and the second-generation iPhone Air, are set to have 24MP front cameras. This represents an upgrade from the 18MP front cameras rumored for the iPhone 17 line. This enhancement aims to boost performance in portrait mode, improve edge detection, and enhance skin tone accuracy.

Economy models like the iPhone 18e and the 17e will likely retain 12MP cameras to maintain affordability.

Also Read: Apple’s Foldable iPhone May Be Cheaper to Make Than Expected

Launch Timeline Remains Uncertain

The timeline for Apple’s foldable iPhone remains a bit murky, as analyst Mark Gurman anticipates its release in the fall of 2026. However, Mizuho Securities speculates a possible delay into 2027 as Apple finalizes important design details, such as the hinge mechanism.

JP Morgan also hints at a strategic shift for Apple starting in 2026, potentially launching high-end models (including the foldable and iPhone 18 Pro series) in the fall, while releasing standard models like the iPhone 18 and 18e in the spring of 2027.

Should these predictions hold, the foldable iPhone might set new standards for under-display technology and influence Apple’s next wave of mobile innovation.

How do you feel about a foldable iPhone with an under-display camera? Share your thoughts below.

title.rendered: Truely eSIM: Travel the World Without Changing Your SIM Card

content.rendered:
Traveling is exciting until you land in a new country and your phone suddenly stops working. You start hunting for Wi-Fi, searching for a local SIM, or paying crazy roaming fees just to stay connected. Sound familiar?

That’s where Truely steps in. It’s a travel eSIM app that lets you use your iPhone to travel the world without ever changing your SIM card. One app, one setup, and you’re connected across 190+ countries.

In this article, I’ll share what Truely is, how it works, and why it’s redefining travel connectivity for global adventurers.

Table of Contents
  • What is Truely Switchless?
  • Key Features That Make Truely Stand Out
    • 1. Global “Switchless®” Connectivity
    • 2. One App to Manage Everything
    • 3. Flexible Data Options
    • 4. Pause & Resume Feature
    • 5. Instant eSIM Activation
    • 6. One-Tap eSIM Compatibility Check
    • 7. Reliable Local Network Partners
    • 8. Helpful Human Support
    • 9. Easy Refunds
  • How Truely Works
  • My Experience with Truely
  • Who Should Get Truely?
  • Final Verdict: Should You Try Truely?

What is Truely Switchless?

Truely is a travel eSIM app that lets you connect to the internet in over 190 countries without switching physical SIM cards.

Instead of juggling multiple local SIMs or paying huge roaming fees, you just install one Truely eSIM profile, and it automatically connects you to 700+ local networks as you move from one country to another.

They call this seamless experience Switchless®, meaning you install once and go global. It’s like taking your home internet connection wherever you go, only lighter, faster, and smarter.

Key Features That Make Truely Stand Out

Here are the features that make Truely one of the most versatile and traveler-friendly eSIM apps available today:

1. Global “Switchless®” Connectivity

Buy a plan, install the eSIM, and go anywhere. Truely automatically connects to the best local networks when crossing borders within the selected country or region-no need to manually switch between them.

2. One App to Manage Everything

Manage your plans, track data usage, top up, or switch to a new region directly within the Truely app. Designed for simplicity, it’s perfect for travelers who prefer a clean, all-in-one solution.

3. Flexible Data Options

Truely offers Unlimited and Pay per GB data options, giving users more flexibility. You can choose between:

  • Unlimited Data Plans (No speed cap up to 5GB, after 5GB unlimited use at 512 Kbps)
  • Pay per GB Packs available in 300MB, 1GB, 5GB, 10GB, and 20GB options, with validity of 2 days, 30 days, or Unlimited.

This feature helps travelers personalize their data usage based on trip length and browsing needs.

4. Pause & Resume Feature

Another traveler-friendly innovation that allows you to save unused data and maximize the value of their purchase. It’s especially useful for multi-country trips or intermittent travel where connectivity isn’t needed every day.

5. Instant eSIM Activation

No more waiting or switching physical SIMs. You can activate your plan ahead of time or upon arrival. Just scan the QR code or use the one-tap install via the app.

6. One-Tap eSIM Compatibility Check

Not sure if your phone supports eSIM? Truely has an eSIM compatibility check right in the app. With a single tap, you can instantly verify device compatibility.

7. Reliable Local Network Partners

Truely partners with 700+ top-tier local carriers worldwide to ensure fast, stable 4G/LTE data wherever possible. You can even share your data via Hotspot or tethering, ideal for laptops and travel companions.

8. Helpful Human Support

Truely’s 24/7 support team is consistently praised for being quick, friendly, and knowledgeable.

9. Easy Refunds

Plans change. Flights get canceled. Destinations switch. Truely offers flexible refund and cancellation policies, giving travelers peace of mind when the unexpected happens.

Along with these useful features, the app has more under the sleeves. Truely plans to offer Share Days where you can send your unused balance to your family or friends. Moreover, they will allow you to buy multiple plans from one account similar to Apple’s Family Sharing.

How Truely Works

Here’s how to go Switchless® with Truely:

  1. Ensure your phone is eSIM capable and unlocked.
  2. You can choose the plans on the Truely website or download the Truely app on your iPhone.
  3. Choose your plan based on country, region, or data preference (Unlimited or Pay per GB).
  4. Use our exclusive promo code to get a 10% discount: IGEEKSBLOG10
  5. Sign up using your email address.
  6. Follow the in-app instructions to install the eSIM.
  7. Activate upon arrival. Truely automatically connects to the best local network.
  8. Browse, map, call, and stream – You’re online before you even reach baggage claim.

My Experience with Truely

What makes Truely stand out for me:

  • Massive coverage (190+ countries)
  • True Switchless® convenience so no local SIM hunting
  • Easy setup and instant top-ups
  • Hotspot/tethering support
  • Fair pricing for multi-country travel
  • Friendly, round-the-clock support

The only caveat: Truely offers data-only plans, so you can’t make traditional voice calls or send SMS. Heavy streamers may also find data caps limiting, though the new Pay per GB option adds welcome flexibility.

Who Should Get Truely?

Given the above, the best fit depends on your travel style.

Ideal for:

  • Frequent travelers hopping between countries
  • You use massive amounts of data for streaming
  • Digital nomads and remote workers
  • People who hate SIM swapping
  • Data-first users relying on WhatsApp, Zoom, Slack, etc.
  • Anyone who values convenience and reliability

Maybe skip if:

  • You need a local phone number or SMS
  • You’re staying long-term in a single country and want the cheapest possible option

Final Verdict: Should You Try Truely?

Absolutely! If you value simplicity, flexibility, and global connectivity, Truely delivers on its “install once, travel anywhere” promise. You get fast data, no SIM juggling or shocking roaming bills from your home carrier, and smooth automatic connectivity.

With its innovative Pay per GB data packs, the Pause & Resume feature, and the one-tap eSIM compatibility check, Truely is raising the bar for what a modern travel eSIM can do. If you’re planning your next trip, go Switchless with Truely and keep your adventures focused on the journey, not your SIM card.

Don’t forget to use our exclusive promo code to get a 10% discount: IGEEKSBLOG10

What do you think about Truely? Let us know in the comments below!

socialPosts.linkedin: Ever been frustrated trying to stay connected abroad, juggling local SIMs or crazy roaming charges? ✈️🌍 Enter Truely — the travel eSIM app that promises seamless, switchless connectivity across 190+ countries. Imagine installing once and never worrying about changing SIM cards again! 🔑 Key takeaways: - Automatic local network switching with Switchless® technology—no manual SIM swaps. - Manage everything easily through one app, from plans to data tracking. - Flexible options like unlimited or pay-per-GB plans, plus features like Pause & Resume for optimal control. As someone who's traveled extensively, the convenience Truely offers resonates deeply. It’s like having your home internet wherever you go—fast, reliable, and hassle-free. What’s your biggest challenge with travel connectivity? Would you try a switchless eSIM? Let’s discuss! Check out the full story and how Truely is redefining global travel connectivity here: IGeeksBlog Truely Review. #TravelTech #eSIM #GlobalConnectivity #DigitalNomad #Innovation

title.rendered: Got a New iPhone? Try These 22 Tips to Use It Like a Pro

content.rendered:
Just got your hands on the all-new iPhone 17? Congratulations! Apple’s latest flagship delivers a sleek design, exceptional performance, and plenty of new features that take the iPhone experience to another level. Whether you’ve switched from Android or upgraded from an older iPhone, there’s a lot to explore.

To help you make the most of your new device, here are 22 must-try iPhone tips and tricks that’ll make you feel like a pro from day one.

Table of Contents
  • Customize AssistiveTouch Gestures
  • Swipe to Type Faster
  • Create Text Replacements
  • Maximize Battery Life
  • Take Selfies Using Headphones
  • Customize Your Control Center
  • Quickly Delete Numbers in Calculator
  • Lock Your iPhone to a Single App
  • Stop Music Automatically with a Timer
  • Measure Objects or Height
  • Set up Back Tap Gestures
  • Save Your Email Signature
  • Make the Most of Siri
  • Unlock your iPhone with Your Voice
  • Stop Apps from Tracking You
  • Bundle and Schedule Notifications
  • Use Live Text
  • Create Custom Shortcuts
  • Change Panorama Directions
  • Access Spotlight Search Anywhere
  • Lock Private Notes
  • Add Widgets to Your Home Screen

    1. Customize AssistiveTouch Gestures

    With AssistiveTouch, you can perform quick actions like taking screenshots or opening the Camera with just one tap.

    Here’s how to take screenshots using AssistiveTouch:

    1. Go to Settings → Accessibility → Touch → AssistiveTouch

    2. Toggle on AssistiveTouch.
    3. Select Single-Tap.
    4. From the options, select Screenshot.
    5. Now, tap the small grey icon to capture your screen instantly. This is just one example. AssistiveTouch can do much more.

    2. Swipe to Type Faster

    Introduced with iOS 13, QuickPath swipe typing lets you glide across letters instead of tapping them. Once you get the hang of it, it’s faster and smoother than traditional typing.

    Try it in any text field by swiping across each letter in a word like “iGeeksBlog” without lifting your finger.

    3. Create Text Replacements  

    If you often type the same phrases, Text Replacement can save you time. For example, you can make “hp” expand into “hyperrealism and Photorealism.”

    Set it up by going to Settings → General → Keyboard → Text Replacement, and add your shortcuts.

    4. Maximize Battery Life

    Battery draining too quickly? Extend your iPhone’s battery life by turning off Location Services, enabling Auto-Brightness, and placing your phone face down when not in use.

    You’ll be surprised how much difference these small changes can make.

    5. Take Selfies Using Headphones

    No selfie stick? No problem. Connect your wired headphones or Bluetooth earbuds, open the Camera, and press the volume button to snap a selfie.

    It’s perfect for hands-free shots or group selfies from a distance.

    6. Customize Your Control Center

    Add your most-used tools to the Control Center for easy access.

    Here’s how you can customize the Control Center on iPhone:

    1. Swipe down from the top right to pull down the Control Center.
    2. Tap the “+” button at the top left corner.
    3. Tap Add a Control at the bottom center..
    4. Select the widget you want to add to the Control Center.
    5. You can also long-press any empty space in the Control Center, then adjust the widget positions and sizes.

    7. Quickly Delete Numbers in Calculator

    Accidentally typed the wrong digit? Just swipe left or right on the number display in the Calculator app to delete the last entry instead of starting over.

    8. Lock Your iPhone to a Single App

    With Guided Access, you can lock your iPhone to one app, which is ideal for lending your phone to kids or guests.

    To set up Guided Access:

    1. Open Settings.
    2. Go to Accessibility.
    3. Scroll down and select Guided Access.
    4. Toggle on Guided Access.

    5. Tap Passcode Settings.
    6. Tap Guided Access Passcode.
      Set your passcode: You’ll need to provide this when turning off Guided Access.
    7. Optional: Toggle on Face ID or Touch ID as an added security for Guided Access.

    Once set up, you can open and lock any app. For instance, open the Photos app. Now, press the side (power) button thrice to activate guided access and lock your iPhone to the Photos app.

    Note: Double-press the side button to switch off Guided Access using Face ID. To use your passcode, press the side button thrice and enter your passcode.

    9. Stop Music Automatically with a Timer

    Set your iPhone to stop playing music after a set time, perfect for bedtime playlists.

    1. Launch the Clock app.
    2. Tap Timer at the bottom right.
    3. Slide the figures to the corresponding hour, minute, and seconds that you want.
    4. Tap When Timer Ends.
    5. Scroll to the bottom and select Stop Playing.
    6. Tap Set at the top right.
    7. Select Start to start timing your music.

    You can now play your music while asleep or busy; the timer will stop it at the specified time.

    10. Measure Objects or Height

    If your iPhone has a LiDAR scanner (iPhone 12 Pro or newer), open the Measure app to check dimensions or even someone’s height using AR.

    11. Set up Back Tap Gestures

    You can assign shortcuts to a double or triple tap on the back of your iPhone.

    To activate gestures for Back Tap:

    1. Open Settings.
    2. Go to Accessibility.
    3. Tap Touch.
    4. Scroll down and select Back Tap.
    5. Here, pick a gesture from the list for the Double Tap or Single Tap action.

    Now, single-tap or double-tap the Apple logo behind your iPhone to see the magic unfold. If you are having trouble setting up Back Tap, try these fixes.

    12. Save Your Email Signature

    Want your email signature added automatically?

    To set up and save your email signature on iPhone:

    1. Open Settings → Apps → Mail.
    2. Here, scroll to the bottom and tap Signature.
    3. Type your signature in the field.
    4. Tap Per Account and Add your Signature.

    Now, try sending a message using the built-in Mail app. Your signature will be added at the end.

    13. Make the Most of Siri

    Siri can do far more than simple searches. You can:

    • How to use Type to Siri on iPhone, iPad and Mac (Apple Intelligence)
    • Get Siri to read emails, articles, and other text on iPhone
    • Use Siri offline on iPhone (without the internet)

    It’s worth exploring these time-saving features in your settings.

    14. Unlock your iPhone with Your Voice

    Although not the most secure option, you can use Voice Control to unlock your iPhone. Here’s how:

    1. Go to Settings → Accessibility.
    2. Select Voice Control.
    3. Toggle on Voice Control.
    4. Tap Customize Commands.

    5. Tap Create New Command.
      Type a phrase or word you can easily remember.
    6. Tap Action and select Run Custom Gesture.


      Ensure that the points you tap correspond to your passcode combinations. Otherwise, this fails.
    7. Tap Save at the top right.

    8. Next, tap New Command at the top left to go back.
    9. Finally, tap Save.

    Now, say the phrase or word you entered earlier to unlock your iPhone. If you forgot your iphone passcode, you can check out our guide.

    15. Stop Apps from Tracking You

    Take control of your privacy by turning off tracking requests.

    Here’s how:

    1. Launch Settings.
    2. Go to Privacy → Select Tracking.
    3. Toggle off Allow Apps to Request to Track.

    To prevent a specific app from tracking you, check out our guide on how to stop iPhone apps from tracking you.

    16. Bundle and Schedule Notifications

    Too many alerts? Use Notification Summary to group them and schedule when they appear.

    Go to Settings → Notifications → Scheduled Summary, and choose the apps and times that work best for you.

    17. Use Live Text

    With Live Text, you can copy text from images or photos and even call phone numbers detected in pictures.

    Just point your camera at text, tap the indicator, and choose “Copy” or “Call.”

    18. Create Custom Shortcuts

    Use the Shortcuts app to automate tasks like turning on Low Power Mode when the battery hits 20% or sending a daily reminder message.

    Check out Apple’s gallery of pre-made shortcuts to get started.

    If you are curious, you can check our in-depth guide on how to create shortcuts on iPhone and iPad.

    19. Change Panorama Directions

    This photographic trick is for those who love to display the beauty around them in a unique dimension. Panoramic photos, when taken professionally, are always worth a stare. They give the world a rounded, unbroken perspective.

    Want to exhibit your panoramic photographic skills using your iPhone? It’s simple:

    1. Launch Camera.
    2. Slide Camera modes at the bottom and select Pano.
    3. Tap the round dot to start recording.
    4. Move your camera slowly along the direction of the arrow.
    5. Tap the arrow to change directions.
    6. Next, tap the stop icon to save the photo.

    20. Access Spotlight Search Anywhere

    Swipe down from the middle of your Home Screen (or within apps) to use Spotlight Search. You can find apps, contacts, files, or even web results without leaving your current screen.

    21. Lock Private Notes

    Keep sensitive notes secure by locking them. In the Notes app, swipe left on a note, tap the lock icon, and set a passcode or Face ID.

    Check out our comprehensive guide on locking the Note app on iPhone or iPad.

    22. Add Widgets to Your Home Screen

    Customize your Home Screen by adding widgets for weather, battery status, or favorite apps.

    1. Long-tap a space on your Home Screen.
    2. Tap the Edit button at the top left corner.
    3. Select Add Widgets in the drop-down menu.
    4. Locate and select the Widget you want to add..
    5. Next, select the widget style and tap the Add Widget button.

    Final thoughts

    Whether you’re new to iPhone or upgrading from an older model, these tricks can help you discover hidden gems and personalize your experience. Try them out and you’ll be surprised how much smoother and smarter your iPhone feels.

    Read more:

    • How to check if you need to replace your iPhone battery
    • Where to sell your old iPhone
    • How to find the owner of a lost or stolen iPhone or iPad
    • How to use T9 dialing on an iPhone

title.rendered: Find Out What iPhone Model You Have: Easy Ways to Identify Your iPhone

content.rendered:
Trying to figure out which iPhone model you own? You’re not alone. With so many generations that look almost identical, it can be tricky to tell them apart at first glance. In this quick guide, we’ll show you the easiest ways to identify your iPhone model whether it’s in your hand or completely powered off. Let’s get started.

Table of Contents
  • Why Knowing Your iPhone Model Matters
  • Method 1: Check Your iPhone Model in Settings
  • Method 2: Find the Model Number Inside the SIM Slot
  • Method 3: Look at the Back of Your iPhone
  • Complete List of Apple's iPhone Model Number
  • Know Your iPhone Better

Why Knowing Your iPhone Model Matters

Knowing your exact iPhone model is useful for several reasons. It helps you confirm compatibility with accessories, ensure your device supports the latest iOS updates, choose the right case or screen protector, and even get the right trade-in or resale value.

Follow the steps below to find your iPhone model number and match it with Apple’s official list.

Method 1: Check Your iPhone Model in Settings

The easiest way to identify your iPhone model is through the Settings app. Here’s how:

  1. Unlock your iPhone and open Settings.
  2. Tap General, then tap About.
  3. Look for Model Name and Model Number.
  4. Tap the model number once. It will change to a number starting with “A” (for example, Axxxx).

That’s your iPhone’s official model number, which you can then match with Apple’s list below.

Method 2: Find the Model Number Inside the SIM Slot

If your iPhone won’t turn on, you can still find the model number. On iPhone 8 and newer models, the model number is etched inside the SIM slot.

  1. Use a SIM ejector tool or paperclip to remove the SIM tray.
  2. Shine a flashlight into the slot and look carefully at the upper side.
  3. You’ll see a small number starting with “A.”

This is your model number.

On newer iPhones that are eSIM-only, you won’t find a SIM tray. Instead, the model number is printed inside the USB-C or Lightning connector, on the upper side (the same side as the display).

Method 3: Look at the Back of Your iPhone

If you have an older iPhone (7 or earlier), the model number is printed directly on the back of the device.

  1. Remove any case or skin from your iPhone.
  2. Look near the bottom of the back. You’ll find a small text that includes the model number starting with “A.”

Apple stopped printing model numbers on the back starting with the iPhone 8, so for newer models, use one of the other methods above.

Complete List of Apple’s iPhone Model Number

Once you’ve found your iPhone’s model number, use this list to identify which iPhone you have.

The iPhone 12 series and earlier models were limited to specific countries, so we have created a list of the iPhone 12 series and iPhone 1 below.

iPhone 12 Pro Max

  • A2342 (United States)
  • A2410 (Canada, Japan)
  • A2412 (China mainland, Hong Kong, Macao)
  • A2411 (other countries and regions)

iPhone 12 Pro

  • A2341 (United States)
  • A2406 (Canada, Japan)
  • A2408 (China mainland, Hong Kong, Macao)
  • A2407 (other countries and regions)

iPhone 12

  • A2172 (United States)
  • A2402 (Canada, Japan)
  • A2404 (China Mainland, Hong Kong, Macao)
  • A2403 (other countries and regions)

iPhone 12 mini

  • A2176 (United States)
  • A2398 (Canada, Japan)
  • A2400 (China mainland)
  • A2399 (other countries and regions)

iPhone SE (2nd generation)

  • A2275 (Canada, United States)
  • A2298 (China mainland)
  • A2296 (other countries and regions)

iPhone 11 Pro Max

  • A2161 (Canada, United States)
  • A2220 (China mainland, Hong Kong, Macao)
  • A2218 (other countries and regions)

iPhone 11 Pro

  • A2160 (Canada, United States)
  • A2217 (China mainland, Hong Kong, Macao)
  • A2215 (other countries and regions)

iPhone 11

  • A2111 (Canada, United States)
  • A2223 (China mainland, Hong Kong, Macao)
  • A2221 (other countries and regions)

iPhone XS Max

  • A1921, A2101
  • A2102 (Japan)
  • A2103
  • A2104 (China mainland)

iPhone XS

  • A1920, A2097
  • A2098 (Japan)
  • A2099
  • A2100 (China mainland)

iPhone XR

  • A1984, A2105
  • A2106 (Japan)
  • A2107
  • A2108 (China mainland)

iPhone X

  • A1865, A1901
  • A1902 (Japan)

iPhone 8 Plus

  • A1864, A1897
  • A1898 (Japan)

  • A1863, A1905
  • A1906 (Japan)

iPhone 7 Plus

  • A1661, A1784
  • A1785 (Japan)

iPhone 7

  • A1660, A1778
  • A1779 (Japan)

iPhone 6s Plus

  • A1634, A1687, A1699

iPhone 6s

  • A1633, A1688, A1700

iPhone SE (1st generation)

  • A1723, A1662, A1724

iPhone 6 Plus

  • A1522, A1524, A1593

iPhone 6

  • A1549, A1586, A1589

iPhone 5s

  • A1453, A1457, A1518, A1528, A1530, A1533

iPhone 5c

  • A1456, A1507, A1516, A1529, A1532

iPhone 5

  • A1428, A1429, A1442

iPhone 4s

  • A1431, A1387

iPhone 4

  • A1349, A1332

iPhone 3GS

  • A1325, A1303

iPhone 3G

  • A1324, A1241

iPhone (The 1st iPhone)

  • A1203

Know Your iPhone Better

That’s how you can easily find out what iPhone you have. Once you know the model number, you can explore more about your device’s specs, features, and update compatibility.

If you found this guide helpful, share it with friends or leave your questions in the comments below.

title.rendered: How to Unlock Your iPhone with Apple Watch (Step-by-Step Guide)

content.rendered:
Apple has made unlocking your iPhone faster and more convenient than ever. Face ID is designed to recognize you instantly, but it can sometimes struggle when you’re wearing sunglasses.If you often keep your shades on, your iPhone might not unlock as smoothly as you’d like.

That’s where your Apple Watch can make a big difference. You can use it to unlock your iPhone automatically, without removing your sunglasses or entering your passcode. Here’s how it works and how to set it up for seamless access.

Table of Contents
  • How Does the Unlock with Apple Watch Feature Work?
  • How to Enable Unlock with Apple Watch on iPhone
  • How to Lock Your iPhone Using Apple Watch
  • Is Unlocking Your iPhone with Apple Watch Secure?
  • Unlock with Apple Watch Not Working? Try These Fixes

How Does the Unlock with Apple Watch Feature Work?

When you enable the Unlock With Apple Watch option on your iPhone, your Apple Watch can automatically unlock your iPhone whenever Face ID struggles to recognize your face.

Once the Apple Watch detects that it has unlocked your iPhone, you’ll get a haptic feedback and notification confirming that your iPhone has been unlocked.

Here’s what happens: if your iPhone detects a face (partially covered by a mask or sunglasses) and your Apple Watch is on your wrist, unlocked, and nearby, your iPhone unlocks instantly. You’ll feel a quick haptic tap on your wrist and see a notification confirming your iPhone has been unlocked.

This feature works on iPhone X or later and Apple Watch Series 3 or newer. Before setting it up, make sure these conditions are met:

  • Both devices are close to each other.
  • Wi-Fi and Bluetooth are enabled on both.
  • Both are signed in with the same Apple ID and have passcodes enabled.
  • Wrist Detection is turned on in the Apple Watch settings.

How to Enable Unlock with Apple Watch on iPhone

Follow these steps to enable the feature:

  1. Open the Settings app on your iPhone and head to Face ID & Passcode settings.
  2. Scroll down to the Unlock with Apple Watch section and toggle on [Your Name] Apple Watch.

That’s it. Now, whenever Face ID can’t identify you, your Apple Watch will unlock your iPhone automatically.

How to Lock Your iPhone Using Apple Watch

Sometimes, your Apple Watch might unlock your iPhone unintentionally for instance, when someone else picks it up while you’re nearby. Apple has thought of that too.

If you get a notification saying your iPhone has been unlocked, tap the Lock iPhone button on your Apple Watch. This immediately re-locks your iPhone and disables Apple Watch unlocking until you manually enter your passcode.

Is Unlocking Your iPhone with Apple Watch Secure?

Yes, it’s very secure. Apple designed this feature with multiple layers of protection:

  • Your Apple Watch must be on your wrist, unlocked, and near your iPhone.
  • Face ID must detect a face before triggering the feature.
  • You receive a haptic alert and notification every time your iPhone is unlocked via Apple Watch.
  • Both devices must be signed in with the same Apple ID, preventing unauthorized access.

This ensures convenience without compromising security.

Watch this quick video guide:

Unlock with Apple Watch Not Working? Try These Fixes

If your Apple Watch isn’t unlocking your iPhone, try these troubleshooting tips:

  • Check that Bluetooth and Wi-Fi are enabled on both devices.
  • Ensure your Apple Watch is unlocked and Wrist Detection is turned on (go to Watch app > Passcode > Wrist Detection).
  • Make sure Face ID for iPhone Unlock is toggled on under Settings > Face ID & Passcode.
  • Restart both your iPhone and Apple Watch to clear minor bugs.

If it still doesn’t work, contact Apple Support for further assistance.

Signing off…

Unlocking your iPhone with your Apple Watch is one of those small but meaningful Apple ecosystem features that make life easier. Whether you’re masked up, wearing sunglasses, or just want faster access, it’s a reliable and secure solution.

If you have a compatible iPhone and Apple Watch, enable this feature today and enjoy seamless unlocking across your devices.

Still have questions? Drop them in the comments, and we’ll be happy to help!

keyPoints.title: Introduction of Mask Unlock on iOS 15.4
keyPoints.explanation: Apple added a feature in iOS 15.4 that allows iPhones to be unlocked with Face ID while wearing a mask, although sunglasses can still prevent it from working.

keyPoints.title: Unlocking iPhone Using Apple Watch
keyPoints.explanation: Users can unlock their iPhone with an Apple Watch if Face ID and masks are problematic, provided the watch is unlocked, on the wrist, and close to the iPhone.

keyPoints.title: Enabling Unlock with Apple Watch
keyPoints.explanation: The feature can be enabled through iPhone Settings under Face ID & Passcode, allowing automatic unlocking when Face ID recognizes a masked face and the Apple Watch is on the wrist.

keyPoints.title: Locking iPhone via Apple Watch
keyPoints.explanation: Users can remotely lock their iPhone from the Apple Watch to prevent unintended unlocking, which disables the feature until re-authenticated with the passcode.

keyPoints.title: Security of Unlock with Apple Watch
keyPoints.explanation: The security is maintained as the feature requires the watch to be on the wrist, unlocked, in proximity, and signed into the same Apple ID, with multiple security layers in place.

title.rendered: Apple Opens Submissions for 2026 Swift Student Challenge

content.rendered:
Apple has kicked off the 2026 Swift Student Challenge, reaching out to budding developers worldwide to put their creativity and coding proficiency on display. The announcement, initially made through Apple’s developer portal, states that the entry window will be open from February 6 to February 28, 2026.

What’s New: 2026 Challenge Details

The Swift Student Challenge is Apple’s yearly contest aimed at motivating student developers to craft interactive app playgrounds using Swift Playgrounds or Xcode. This initiative seeks to showcase innovative ideas and inspire future tech industry leaders.

As outlined by Apple, submissions will be evaluated based on several criteria: innovation, creativity, social impact, and inclusivity. Selected entries will earn the prestigious title of Distinguished Winners. These winners will be invited for a summer visit to Apple’s headquarters in Cupertino, California, with Apple covering travel and accommodation costs.

During their trip, winners are usually granted access to Apple’s Worldwide Developers Conference (WWDC), anticipated in June 2026. Here, attendees might see the unveiling of Apple’s forthcoming software lineup, including iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, watchOS 27, tvOS 27, and visionOS 27.

Free Learning Sessions for Aspiring Developers

In preparation for submissions, Apple is offering free online learning sessions aimed at equipping students with the necessary skills to develop their projects. These workshops feature:

  • Code-along: Start building with Swift and SwiftUI – November 14, 2025
  • Get ready for the Swift Student Challenge – January 15, 2026
  • Code-along: Experiment with coding intelligence in Xcode 26 – February 5, 2026

Led by Apple experts, these sessions are intended to guide students throughout the app creation process—from brainstorming ideas to designing and fine-tuning their playgrounds. Apple is also encouraging participants to tackle real-world issues and drive positive change within their communities.

Participation Guidelines and Recognition

Apple specifies that eligible developers can participate in the challenge a maximum of three times. All winners receive official recognition alongside exclusive Apple merchandise, while Distinguished Winners are rewarded with the special trip to Apple Park.

The company continues to spotlight previous winners’ stories, showcasing how their coding skills have brought about change—ranging from accessibility-enhancing apps to innovative educational and sustainability tools.

Students interested in participating can access detailed information, eligibility requirements, and resources on Apple’s official Swift Student Challenge webpage.

How does this apply to you? Share your thoughts below.

title.rendered: Next iPhone Air Could Finally Fix Its Camera Problem

content.rendered:
Apple looks set to finally address one of the biggest complaints about the iPhone Air: its lone rear camera. A fresh report from Digital Chat Station on Weibo indicates that Apple is exploring a dual-camera configuration for the upcoming iPhone Air, poised for a 2026 debut alongside the iPhone 18 lineup.

Dual-Camera Setup Could Enhance iPhone Air’s Capabilities

While the current iPhone Air impressed many with its ultra-thin profile, the single rear camera has turned off some potential buyers who desire multiple lenses. The next iteration, which is being referred to as the iPhone 18 Air, might include dual 48MP sensors: a main Fusion camera and a Fusion ultra-wide lens. This would bring its photo capabilities closer to those of the baseline iPhone 17.

That said, it might still miss out on a telephoto lens, an offering reserved for the iPhone Pro models. As a result, while landscape and group shots may become more versatile, optical zoom won’t be part of the package. Nonetheless, a second lens would represent a giant leap in the iPhone Air’s camera game without sacrificing its sleek aesthetic.

Same Slim Look, Bigger Internal Challenge

There’s speculation that Apple intends to retain the iPhone Air’s horizontal camera plateau. This choice is seen as a strategy to optimize battery capacity inside the device’s sleek frame. It’s expected that the additional camera lens would be incorporated alongside the main one within the current setup, avoiding a switch to the vertical arrangement seen in the iPhone 17.

This plan brings engineering hurdles. Integrating another 48MP sensor in such a compact device might push Apple to rethink internal design and heat management. Despite the challenges, Apple’s aim appears unchanged: to keep the featherweight, ultra-slim profile while enhancing functionality.

Release Expected in Late 2026

Industry analyst Ming-Chi Kuo suggests that the next iPhone Air will likely see the light of day in the latter half of 2026, launching alongside the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and Apple’s inaugural foldable iPhone. Reports also mention a larger iPhone Air model in the works for 2027, signalling an expanded lineup.

Thus far, the existing iPhone Air hasn’t fared well outside China, if prior reports are accurate. Apple’s decision to enhance its camera might be a strategy to rekindle global interest, aiming to harmonize cutting-edge design with improved photography.

Leak Source With a Reliable Track Record

Digital Chat Station is no stranger to accurate Apple leaks, having previously disclosed significant details about the camera sensors for the iPhone 15 and the display design of the iPhone 12. While product plans could still shift ahead of launch, if this leak holds true, it suggests Apple is keen on making the iPhone Air more than just a fashion-forward device—one that could finally marry style with substance.

Would an upgrade like this catch your interest? Share your thoughts below.

title.rendered: Snapchat’s Imagine Lens: Create Anything You Can Describe

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • What is the Imagine Lens on Snapchat: The Imagine Lens uses generative AI and AR to turn text prompts into creative visuals directly within your Snaps.
  • How to use the Imagine Lens: Open Snapchat, tap the AI+ button, enter or edit the suggested prompt, then generate, customize, and share your AI-made image.
  • How it differs from filters: Unlike basic filters that overlay effects, Imagine Lens builds entirely new visuals from your ideas, merging AI creativity with your camera.
  • Availability and access limits: It’s currently free for U.S. users and Snapchat Plus subscribers elsewhere, with daily generation caps for non-Platinum plans.

Snapchat has always been known for pushing creativity to new heights with its AR lenses, but its new AI-powered Imagine Lens takes things up a notch. The new tool transforms your everyday Snaps into visuals you could only imagine before, simply by typing a prompt. Whether you want to see yourself as a superhero, a fantasy character, or in a completely different world, Snapchat’s Imagine Lens can make it happen instantly.

Keep reading to learn everything you need to know about the Imagine Lens on Snapchat.

Table of Contents
  • What is the Imagine Lens on Snapchat?
  • How to Use the Imagine Lens on Snapchat
  • Why It’s Different
  • Availability and Access
  • Why Creators Will Love It
  • Bringing Imagination to Reality

What is the Imagine Lens on Snapchat?

Imagine Lens is an AI-powered Snapchat feature that uses generative AI to turn your ordinary Snaps into imaginative visuals using just a few words. Instead of applying a filter before capturing, you take a photo Snap and then use the Imagine Lens to reimagine it into something unique based on a text prompt.

The tool is powered by Snap’s in-house AI model and combines artificial intelligence with augmented reality to produce personalized, creative effects directly in the app.

How to Use the Imagine Lens on Snapchat

Before you try the Imagine Lens on Snapchat, make sure you have an active Snapchat Plus or Platinum subscription.

  1. Open Snapchat and make sure you are on the Camera tab.
  2. Now, take a photo snap like you normally do.
  3. Once done, look for the AI+ (Imagine Lens) button in the right vertical toolbar, and tap it.
  4. Next, Snapchat will automatically suggest a creative prompt based on your Snap. You can use that suggestion or replace it with your own idea, such as “me as an astronaut” or “a painting of my dog.”
  5. Snapchat’s AI will process the image and transform your Snap based on your description. Image generation can take anywhere from an instant to a few seconds, depending on the complexity of your prompt.
  6. Tap Done and you can now edit it, add a caption, save it to your Memories, and share it with your friends or post it to Stories.

Once you share your Snap or post it to Stories, recipients and viewers can reuse your prompt.

Why It’s Different

Unlike regular Snapchat filters, which simply overlay a pre-made effect on your snaps, Imagine Lens creates a completely new visual output from scratch using your Snap and prompt. Each result is one of a kind and a blend of your creativity and the power of AI.

Key highlights:

  • Generates unique visuals after capturing
  • Lets you describe what you want to see
  • Produces results in seconds, right inside the app

Availability and Access

Imagine Lens is part of Snapchat’s AI Creative Tools suite and, at the time of writing, is free for U.S users and only available to Snapchat Plus subscribers in other regions. But even for Snapchat+ users, there’s a limit to how many AI images you can generate each day. A dialog box asking you to get a Lens+ subscription appears when the daily limit is reached. Only Snapchat Platinum subscribers enjoy unlimited generations.

Besides this, since the feature is gaining popularity, we may see Snapchat expanding it to even non-Snapchat Plus users soon.

If you’re a Snapchat Plus user but don’t have access to Imagine Lens, make sure it’s available in your region and that your app is updated to the latest version.

Why Creators Will Love It

Snapchat’s Imagine Lens is a perfect example of how AI and AR can work together to make everyday Snaps more expressive. For creators, it opens up new ways to:

  • Create distinctive, AI-enhanced content
  • Engage audiences with visual storytelling
  • Explore creative ideas without third-party tools

Bringing Imagination to Reality

And that’s about everything you need to know about the Imagine Lens on Snapchat. No longer do you need to rely on filters and lenses created by others; all you need to do is just take a Snap, add a prompt, and let your imagination run wild.

Tried it already? Share your most creative Imagine Lens Snap in the comments.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: HomePod Not Responding? 8 Quick Fixes That Work

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Common reasons HomePod stops responding include power issues, poor Wi-Fi, disabled Siri, gesture bugs, or a frozen OS needing a reboot.
  • Check power and status using the Home app by tapping the HomePod tile—if it says “Playing,” try unplugging for 10 seconds to restart.
  • Look for Home app alerts or warning banners that signal Wi-Fi disconnects, sync errors, or firmware problems affecting HomePod’s behavior.
  • Confirm HomePod is on strong, matching Wi-Fi by checking it shares the same network as your iPhone, with no nearby interference from other devices.
  • Ensure Siri is toggled on for HomePod commands by enabling “Listen for Siri” and “Touch and Hold” in Home settings, with correct language selected.

If your HomePod suddenly stops responding, you’re not alone. Whether it’s ignoring “Hey Siri” or touch controls, failing to show up in the Home app, or just feeling a bit sluggish, the fix is usually easier than it seems. In this guide, I’ll explain why your HomePod isn’t responding and share practical steps you can take to get it working again.

Table of Contents
  • Why is My HomePod Not Responding to Voice Commands or Touch Controls?
  • 8 Methods to Fix HomePod Not Responding
    • 1. Ensure HomePod is Turned On
    • 2. Check For the Alerts in the Home App
    • 3. Connect HomePod to a Strong Wi-Fi Connection
    • 4. Make Sure Siri is Enabled for HomePod
    • 5. Restart HomePod
    • 6. Confirm HomePod Firmware is Updated
    • 7. Remove & Re-Add the HomePod
    • 8. Manual Hardware Reset
    • Contact Apple Support
  • Fix Your HomePod Quickly!

Why is My HomePod Not Responding to Voice Commands or Touch Controls? 

When a HomePod ignores Hey Siri or doesn’t react when you tap the top surface, the cause is usually one of the following things: 

  • The HomePod isn’t powered on 
  • Software crash causing a boot loop 
  • Siri is disabled or can’t hear you 
  • No active internet connection 
  • There’s a gesture-recognition glitch 
  • Updates stuck midway, or Home app sync issues 
  • Interference with home hubs or paired devices 
  • Hardware failure 

For this reason, you may see a No Response alert for your HomePod or HomePod mini in the Home app.

8 Methods to Fix HomePod Not Responding

Try these proven methods to fix your unresponsive HomePod in minutes.

1. Ensure HomePod is Turned On

It might happen, you’re continuously calling Siri, but HomePod isn’t responding because you haven’t actually turned it on! You can make sure it’s powered on by tapping the top surface. A pulsing white light will show.  

Otherwise, open the Home app on your iPhone/iPad and tap on the HomePod. Check if it shows as ‘Playing’ when you initiate music. If it fails even this basic step, power-cycle the speaker before moving to the next step.  

  1. Switch the HomePod off and unplug it from the wall outlet. 
  2. Now, wait for 10 seconds. 
  3. Plug the HomePod back in securely and turn it on. You may try a different power outlet. 

Now, check if it responds to your voice commands or touch controls. 

2. Check For the Alerts in the Home App

If your HomePod or HomePod mini is having trouble connecting to your home Wi-Fi network, accessing your Apple Account, or experiencing another issue, you will see a warning with details in the Home app. 

  1. Go to the Home app on your iPhone.
  2. Tap HomePod, and you will see an alert banner at the top if it’s not responding or has any issues. 
  3. Select View Details to learn about the problem.  

This step ensures you follow the proper troubleshooting steps and quickly fix your HomePod.

3. Connect HomePod to a Strong Wi-Fi Connection

Your HomePod automatically connects to the same Wi-Fi network as your iPhone. If you’ve recently changed your Wi-Fi password or moved it to another location, you might lose connection. In this case, when you approach Siri, it will tell you that there’s a problem connecting to the Wi-Fi. 

You can also manually verify if there’s a Wi-Fi connection issue from the Home app and connect it to the same network as your iPhone.  

  1. In the Home app, go to the HomePod tab. 
  2. You will see a HomePod Network Mismatch alert.
  3. Tap View Details on the banner. It will show you the Wi-Fi network your iPhone is connected to.
  4. Select Move HomePod to [Wi-Fi network], then wait for the update to complete. 

No network mismatch? Then maybe your Wi-Fi is the culprit. To validate this: 

  1. Open the Home app > HomePod, then tap the Settings icon at the bottom. 
  2. Scroll down to the Wi-Fi Network. Check the Wi-Fi signal strength indicator on the right.  

Your Wi-Fi signal is poor if the signal strength indicator displays two bars or fewer. Eliminate potential Wi-Fi interference sources, such as microwaves or cordless phones, and try relocating your HomePod closer to your router.

4. Make Sure Siri is Enabled for HomePod 

Now that your HomePod and iPhone are connected to the same Wi-Fi network, long-press the top of your HomePod and ask, “Hey Siri, what’s the temperature?” If there’s no response, Siri might be disabled or not listening to you properly. 

  1. In the Home app, tap the HomePod tile, then tap the Settings icon. Tap Listen for “Siri” or “Hey Siri” and choose “Siri” or “Hey Siri.” 
  2. Toggle on Touch and Hold for Siri and Personal Requests. Check for Siri language settings as well. 

Now, try some Siri commands in a clear and loud voice. If your HomePod is still not responding, the microphone may be blocked. Check for any physical obstructions and clean your HomePod.

5. Restart HomePod

Software bugs can cause HomePod to become unresponsive, interrupting its functions. To clear out such software glitches, simply restart the device. It’s a simple yet proven method. 

  1. Open HomePod Settings in the Home app. 
  2. Scroll down to the bottom and tap Reset HomePod. 
  3. Select Restart HomePod from the pop-up. 

6. Confirm HomePod Firmware is Updated 

Apple regularly releases new firmware versions to keep the HomePod working smoothly. By default, those updates happen over the air. You can still verify if any updates are pending. 

  1. Open the Home app and tap the three-dot icon at the top. 
  2. Select Home Settings > Software Update.  
  3. If an update is available, tap Update next to HomePod.  
  4. Also, ensure HomePod is toggled on under Automatic Updates. 
  5. You will see a spinning white light on the top until the installation is finished. 

7. Remove & Re-Add the HomePod 

If your HomePod is still struggling to respond, you need to do a factory reset. This can resolve corrupted settings, network handoffs, or hub registration issues. 

  1. Access Home app > HomePod > Settings icon.  
  2. Tap Reset HomePod at the bottom and select Remove Accessory.
  3. Hit Remove to reset it. 
  4. A white light will start spinning on the top. Wait until it disappears to know the reset is done. 
  5. Then set up HomePod again as if new. Bring your iPhone near and follow the on-screen instructions. 

8. Manual Hardware Reset 

If everything else fails and you’re unable to reset it through the Home app, you can do a full hardware reset: 

  1. Unplug HomePod, wait for ~10 seconds, plug it back in. 
  2. After 10 seconds, touch and hold the top surface. The white light will spin. Continue holding until you see a red light. 
  3. Now, Siri will announce that your HomePod will be reset. Lift your finger once you hear three beeps. 
  4. Once reset, set it up again.

Contact Apple Support 

If, after all these steps, your HomePod still doesn’t respond or function, it may indicate a hardware fault or deeper software corruption that needs service. The best possible way is to contact Apple Support. 

Fix Your HomePod Quickly! 

As HomePod offers much more than just a music-streaming speaker, you might lose productivity on your daily tasks. But we hope you have resolved the error with one of the ways we’ve explained. If yes, then which is it? Tell us about it in the comment section below!

You may also like to read these

  • How to Use HomePod as an Intercom: A Complete Guide
  • How to use HomePod temperature and humidity sensors
  • How to Use Apple Music Crossfade on Any Device

keyPoints.title: Why is My HomePod Not Responding to Voice Commands or Touch Controls?
keyPoints.explanation: Common causes include the device not being powered on, software crashes, Siri disabled, poor internet connection, gesture glitches, app sync issues, interference, or hardware failure.

keyPoints.title: Ensure HomePod is Turned On
keyPoints.explanation: Check for a pulsing white light on top when tapping it; if it shows as 'Playing' in the Home app, power-cycle the device by unplugging it for 10 seconds and reconnecting.

keyPoints.title: Check for Alerts in the Home App
keyPoints.explanation: Visit the Home app to see if there are warning banners or alerts related to connectivity or other issues that need attention.

keyPoints.title: Connect HomePod to a Strong Wi-Fi Connection
keyPoints.explanation: Verify that your HomePod is connected to the same Wi-Fi as your iPhone, with good signal strength, and ensure there are no interference sources nearby.

keyPoints.title: Make Sure Siri is Enabled for HomePod
keyPoints.explanation: In the Home app, check the settings for Siri activation, toggle on 'Listen for Siri', 'Touch and Hold', and ensure the language settings are correct.
