title.rendered: 20 Aesthetic Ocean Wallpapers for iPhone in 4K

content.rendered:
Looking to give your iPhone a fresh and tropical vibe? Whether you love calm blue waves, golden sunsets over the sea, or deep ocean vibes, these ocean wallpapers will make your iPhone screen look straight out of a beach holiday. 

In this collection, we’ve handpicked the best 4K ocean wallpapers, all completely free to download. So, you can enjoy stunning sea views anytime you unlock your phone.

Table of Contents
  • Stunning 4K Ocean Wallpapers for iPhone
    • 1. Beautiful Underwater Ocean
    • 2. Sea Turtle Swimming
    • 3. Peaceful Sunset by the Sea
    • 4. Jumping Dolphin
    • 5. Yellow Surfboard on Black Shore
    • 6. Sailboat at Sunset
    • 7. Diver in the Deep Underwater
    • 8. Beach View of Cliffside
    • 9. Soft Waves on Sand
    • 10. Aerial Beach View
    • 11. Dramatic Ocean Edge
    • 12. Golden Shoreline
    • 13. Soft Sunset Landscape
    • 14. Scenic Ocean Drive
    • 15. Long Coastline
    • 16. Tropical Island View
    • 17. Black Sand Beach
    • 18. Rocky Ocean Coast
    • 19. Dramatic Cliffside
    • 20. Blue Horizon Waves
  • Refresh Your iPhone Screen with Ocean Vibes!

Stunning 4K Ocean Wallpapers for iPhone

Each wallpaper has a unique soothing look and is perfectly sized for any iPhone screen. Explore the collection to the end, then tap the Download button to save the wallpaper in high quality on your device.

1. Beautiful Underwater Ocean

An intriguing shot from under the ocean, with sunlight shining through the water. Every time I unlock my iPhone, it reminds me of my dream of deep-sea diving.  

Download

2. Sea Turtle Swimming

A rare sea turtle that swims gracefully across the crystal blue waters. Since you may never have a real-life opportunity to see it, let it stay on your iPhone screen. 

Download

3. Peaceful Sunset by the Sea

Soft pastel skies, gentle waves, and a bird strolling by the shore-this beach wallpaper captures the quiet beauty of an ocean sunset in 4K. 

Download

4. Jumping Dolphin

Brighten up your screen with this friendly dolphin jumping out of the bright blue water. It adds a fun, refreshing ocean vibe to your lock screen. 

Download

5. Yellow Surfboard on Black Shore

It is a great option if you want black wallpaper. A bright yellow surfboard on a black seashore, this wallpaper is clean, bold, and just so stylish. 

Download

6. Sailboat at Sunset

A colorful boat sailing across calm waters under a glowing orange sunset. This nature wallpaper has a warm and peaceful ocean vibe that is perfect for sunset lovers. 

Download

7. Diver in the Deep Underwater 

Want some water sports adventure? A diver explores a stunning underwater cave, illuminated by glowing blue light and lined with rocky walls. 

Download

8. Beach View of Cliffside

Soft waves meet golden sand beneath towering cliffs and misty skies. It’s perfect for giving your iPhone a refreshing coastal look. 

Download

9. Soft Waves on Sand 

Gentle waves roll onto dark sand, creating a relaxed, peaceful seaside mood. Tap the download button and save this calm ocean look. 

Download

10. Aerial Beach View 

A stunning top-down view of turquoise-colored water meeting soft, sand-filled shores. Complement your iPhone’s Dynamic Island with this wallpaper. 

Download

11. Dramatic Ocean Edge

Looking for a minimal wallpaper to set as your Lock Screen? The striking aerial view shows white waves crashing against rugged black rocks. 

 

Download

12. Golden Shoreline 

A classic golden sand beach with bright turquoise waves fills your iPhone screen. This feels warm and bold! 

Download

13. Soft Sunset Landscape 

Another beautiful landscape wallpaper for your iPhone, featuring soft waves crossing rugged rocks in a warm, peach-colored sunset sky. 

Download

14. Scenic Ocean Drive 

Soft evening light, serene blue water, and a glowing road that curves along the coastline form a serene, dreamlike scene. 

Download

15. Long Coastline 

Aerial view of soft waves onto a long sandy beach at sunset. Add this 4K wallpaper for a calm, aesthetically pleasing look on your iPhone screen. 

Download

16. Tropical Island View 

Keep your iPhone in beach vacation mode with this tropical wallpaper. It shows a small island surrounded by bright turquoise water under a clear sky with soft clouds.  

Download

17. Black Sand Beach 

Waves wash over a striking black-sand beach with a lone palm tree standing near the shore. This gives your iPhone a bold and one-of-a-kind beach look. 

Download

18. Rocky Ocean Coast 

If you want a bold mix of colors and textures, this wallpaper is ideal. Featuring a raw, natural coastal feel, this pairs very well with the iOS 26 design. 

Download

19. Dramatic Cliffside 

Below steep, rugged cliffs lies a wide sandy beach with soft blue water washing gently along the shoreline. It’s a scenic look with a touch of adventure. 

Download

20. Blue Horizon Waves 

Finally, here’s a soothing wallpaper perfect for the Liquid Glass UI. Get an open ocean view with soft waves rolling toward the shore under a pastel sky.  

Download

Refresh Your iPhone Screen with Ocean Vibes! 

Ocean wallpapers are one of the easiest ways to give your iPhone a refreshing, calming, and stylish look. We have tried to include beach waves, dramatic cliffs, underwater scenes, and beautiful sunsets in this collection. So, you can find your perfect lock screen companion. 

If you enjoyed this collection, feel free to bookmark the page or share it with someone who loves sea-themed wallpapers. And stay tuned for more stunning 4K wallpaper collections!

Meanwhile, enjoy these nature-inspired wallpapers:

  • 10 Adorable and Cute Stitch Wallpapers for iPhone
  • Best sunset wallpapers for iPhone to download
  • Best drippy wallpapers for iPhone

title.rendered: Nintendo Store App Arrives on iPhone

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Nintendo Store app now live on iPhone and iPad bringing a unified mobile storefront and fan hub to users across North America, Europe, and Latin America.
  • Lets you browse Switch and Switch 2 gear including physical and digital games, consoles, and merch—though checkout still redirects to the web.
  • View your full Nintendo play history from Switch, 3DS, and Wii U since 2020 by signing in with your Nintendo Account in the app.
  • News alerts, sales notifications, and rewards make it more than a store, doubling as a companion app for Nintendo’s growing lifestyle ecosystem.
  • Can’t make purchases directly in-app so be ready to finish transactions through your browser once you tap checkout.

Nintendo has brought its anticipated Nintendo Store app to iPhone and iPad, creating an easier way for fans to engage with their beloved games and consoles. With the app, the Nintendo eShop is now more accessible to mobile users, complemented by a few features that enthusiasts will find appealing.

Nintendo Store App Now on iPhone, iPad, and Android

Previously available only in Japan under the name My Nintendo for almost five years, the app has been introduced globally with the new title, Nintendo Store. Users in territories like the United States, Canada, Mexico, Brazil, the UK, and much of Europe can now access it on iOS and Android platforms.

Through this app, users are able to browse Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 consoles, in addition to digital and physical games, accessories, and branded merchandise. While actual purchases still occur via Nintendo’s web platform, the app redirects users to a browser for checkout, the browsing process is notably more efficient than manually navigating the website.

View Your Game History Across Consoles

A notable feature of the app is the ability to check your play activity across different Nintendo systems. By signing in with a Nintendo Account, users can review their gaming data for the Switch and Switch 2, and even delve into past play records from Nintendo 3DS and Wii U consoles as far back as February 2020. This function allows players, for the first time, to conveniently access their comprehensive gaming history without relying on parental control apps or third-party solutions.

Also Read: How to use Nintendo Joy-Cons with iPhone, iPad, Apple TV

News, Rewards, and Notifications for Fans

Beyond acting as a storefront, the app functions as a central hub for Nintendo fans. Users can:

  • Stay updated with news about upcoming games and events
  • Receive alerts when items on their wish list go on sale
  • Collect rewards by checking in at official Nintendo locations or events

These features enhance the app beyond just being an online store, transforming it into part of Nintendo’s expanding lineup of lifestyle apps, which includes Nintendo Music and Nintendo Today.

Available Now Worldwide

The Nintendo Store app is accessible free of charge on the App Store and Google Play Store. In Japan, it takes the place of the older My Nintendo app introduced in 2020. With this worldwide release, Nintendo is working to unify its mobile outreach and provide players with a single location for exploring products, staying informed, and tracking their gaming statistics, all directly from their mobile devices.

Ultimately, it’s a modest yet meaningful advance that brings Nintendo fans closer to their favorite games, without needing a console in hand.

Does this update resonate with you? Share your thoughts below.

excerpt.rendered: Nintendo brings its global Store app to iPhone and Android, uniting shopping, gaming history, and news in one sleek mobile experience.

title.rendered: M5 Ultra Chip to Power Mac Studio in 2026

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple skipped the M4 Ultra entirely due to the M4 Max lacking the UltraFusion connector, making a dual-chip Ultra configuration impossible this generation.
  • M5 Ultra likely debuts with 2026 Mac Studio as Apple aligns its chip tiers—base, Pro, Max, and Ultra—within the M5 family for simpler Mac lineup clarity.
  • Mac Pro may get long-overdue upgrade with the M5 Ultra replacing the aging M2 Ultra, bringing both pro desktops onto the same Apple silicon cycle.
  • No major design overhaul expected for the 2026 Mac Studio, but Apple is reportedly developing two new displays, possibly launching alongside the new model.
  • Next Ultra chip could land by WWDC 2026 or fall 2026, but only if Apple hits timeline targets for M5 Pro and Max rollout in early 2026.

Apple seems to be planning an M5 Ultra chip debut for the next Mac Studio iteration scheduled for 2026, based on insights from Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. Gurman’s recent report sheds light on Apple’s forthcoming Mac strategy.

Apple Prepares M5 Ultra for Mac Studio and Possibly Mac Pro

Bloomberg hints that Apple intends to equip the Mac Studio with the M5 Ultra, with a possible rollout to a future Mac Pro also on the table. The M5 Ultra is set to be the premium member of the M5 chipset line, following the expected M5 Pro and M5 Max. Typically, Apple releases its Ultra chips several months after the Max version, suggesting we might wait until mid-to-late 2026 for its release.

At present, the M5 chip can already be found in the latest MacBook Pro and iPad Pro models, which hit stores earlier this year. The anticipated launch of the M5 Pro and M5 Max is early 2026, potentially gearing up the M5 Ultra for an appearance at WWDC 2026 or by fall that year.

Apple Skipped the M4 Ultra: Why That Matters

Apple’s choice to bypass developing an M4 Ultra wasn’t missed by industry professionals and heavy users alike. This year’s Mac Studio updates introduced M4 Max and M3 Ultra options, mixing chip generations and sparking confusion about which fits specific user needs best.

The lack of an M4 Ultra comes down to technical constraints. The M4 Max chip was missing the UltraFusion connector needed to pair two Max units into an Ultra configuration. As Bloomberg reports, Apple doesn’t intend to launch an Ultra variant with every chip genus, choosing instead to focus on significant advances where technology and performance benefits align.

The M5 Ultra Could Fix Apple’s Mixed Chip Lineup

Should Apple release the M5 Ultra, it might streamline its chip lineup by including all variations—base, Pro, Max, and Ultra—within a single generation. This alignment could simplify customer decisions and the overall Mac range. Expectations for the Mac Studio with M5 Ultra center on substantial internal enhancements rather than cosmetic redesigns.

What to Expect from the 2026 Mac Studio

Rumors about a dramatic redesign for the next Mac Studio remain unsubstantiated. However, Bloomberg has noted that Apple is working on two new external displays, with one potentially being unveiled alongside the M5 Ultra Mac Studio. This plan follows Apple’s pattern of launching fresh displays with Mac Studio updates.

If the M5 Ultra also makes its way into the Mac Pro, it would replace the lagging M2 Ultra, which currently powers the existing $6,999 Mac Pro. Skipping the M4 generation might help synchronize both desktop Mac lines with Apple’s silicon development roadmap.

Does this news impact your plans? Share your thoughts below.

title.rendered: 7 Best AI Browsers You Should Try Now

content.rendered:
AI has come a long way from being locked inside a chat box. Today, it’s taking over the very place you spend most of your online time: your browser. With a few prompts, these new AI browsers can plan your trip, summarize research, compare products, or even fill out forms while you sit back.

Most come packed with assistants, task automation, and summarization features, but not every browser gives the same experience. Each has its own personality, unique strengths, and a different AI model powering it. After trying them all, here are the best AI browsers worth your attention.

Table of Contents
  • 7 Best AI Browsers
    • 1. ChatGPT Atlas – Best for Deep Research and Automation
    • 2. Perplexity Comet – Best for Autonomous Browsing and Accuracy
    • 3. Microsoft Edge (Copilot) – Best for Microsoft Office Apps
    • 4. Brave (Leo) – Best for Privacy and Local AI Processing
    • 5. Dia Browser – Best for Personalized and Contextual Browsing
    • 6. Sigma AI Browser – Best for Creators and Content Makers
    • 7. Fellou AI – Best for Task Automation and Data Scraping
  • Final Thoughts

Before we dive deeper, here’s a quick glance at every major AI browser and what each one does best:

7 Best AI Browsers

Agentic AI browsers can browse, book, and even buy things for you. But that power comes with responsibility. Some, like Perplexity Comet, have faced vulnerabilities where hidden web content could manipulate the AI’s actions. It’s a reminder to always review permissions and avoid letting automated modes handle sensitive information. Stick to trusted browsers and use incognito or local modes when privacy matters.

1. ChatGPT Atlas – Best for Deep Research and Automation

ChatGPT is built right into the browser, so you don’t need any extensions or extra tabs. The sidebar understands what’s on your screen, whether it’s an article, dashboard, or PDF, and you can instantly ask follow-up questions without copying or pasting anything. It even remembers what you were doing earlier. With Browser Memories, you can say things like, “Reopen the recipes I found yesterday,” and it’ll pull them right back up.

Agent Mode is where the browser starts feeling like an actual assistant. It can navigate sites, fill out forms, compare products, or add items to a cart with your permission. For example, you can plan a full trip from start to finish, like searching for destinations, building an itinerary, and adding bookings to your cart, all within the same chat. However, the tech is very new and can only handle small tasks, and sometimes gets things wrong. 

Pricing & availability:

  • Free: core browsing + ChatGPT sidebar with limits
  • Plus: ₹1,699/month (≈ $20) for Agent Mode and higher limits
  • Pro: ₹16,500/month (≈ $200) for max limits and fastest models
  • Platforms: macOS now; Windows/iOS/Android “coming soon”

2. Perplexity Comet – Best for Autonomous Browsing and Accuracy

Comet comes with a Perplexity assistant, and as expected, it’s excellent at research. It opens pages, reads through them, follows links, and gives clear, cited answers. It can compare laptops, find the cheapest flight that includes baggage, or provide a quick brief on any niche topic.

However, like with any AI model, you should always cross-verify the information. In our tests, the research, information, and summaries provided by Perplexity were more accurate than those from other models.

It also includes an Agent Mode that can perform small tasks inside the browser, such as booking a table or comparing multiple products. While it works well for most tasks, ChatGPT’s Atlas is a better choice if agentic actions are your main priority. Apart from that, Comet offers small quality-of-life improvements, such as an ad-free experience, split-screen mode, and a familiar interface that feels natural if you’re coming from Chrome.

Pricing & availability:

  • Free (as of Oct 2, 2025): core browser + agentic actions
  • Comet Plus/Max: paid tiers for faster models and priority
  • Platforms: macOS, Windows

3. Microsoft Edge (Copilot) – Best for Microsoft Office Apps

After the release of Atlas and Comet, Microsoft quickly stepped up its game with the Edge browser by introducing Copilot in the sidebar. For the most part, it does exactly what Atlas and Comet do — research, summarize, and perform tasks. However, we noticed that Microsoft’s AI model truly shines at handling tasks with Office products such as Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams, and OneDrive.

You can convert copied data into a clean Excel sheet, adjust formatting for an entire document with a single prompt, or draft professional replies in Outlook. During meetings, Copilot can even read your recap notes in Teams and automatically extract action items, saving you the time of sorting them manually. If your work revolves around these tools, the Edge browser might be your best bet for automating tasks.

Pricing & availability:

  • Free inside Edge for basics; enhanced features via Microsoft 365 plans
  • Platforms: Windows, macOS, iOS, Android

4. Brave (Leo) – Best for Privacy and Local AI Processing

All the previous browsers require you to sign in with your account and stay connected to their servers at all times. Every prompt or data pulled from your tabs is sent to the company’s servers, raising privacy concerns for many users. Brave’s Leo AI doesn’t need an account and keeps everything local by default.

You can switch between models like Mixtral, Claude, and Llama, or connect Ollama to run local models entirely offline. It can summarize web pages, translate text, and even assist with coding, all without sending your data to external servers.

Since there’s no server-side history and Leo uses reverse-proxy anonymization, your activity remains private. Its Bring Your Own Model (BYOM) support makes it ideal for handling sensitive or confidential work. However, Leo is currently designed for research and summarization; it cannot perform tasks or take actions on your behalf yet.

For Privacy, you can also consider the DuckDuckGo browser, which includes DuckDuckBot and Duck.ai for chat or browsing the internet.

Pricing & availability:

  • Free tier: Leo Premium ~ $14.99/month for higher limits/models
  • Platforms: Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android

5. Dia Browser – Best for Personalized and Contextual Browsing

Dia is built from the ground up as an AI-native browser, so every part of it revolves around intelligence and automation. The address bar doubles as a chat window, where you can ask questions, summarize pages, or trigger saved actions. These reusable commands, called Skills, make tasks like “/track-price iPhone 15” or “/find flights to Tokyo” instant and repeatable.

Its Memory feature learns your writing tone, browsing habits, and preferences to personalize how it interacts with you. It can handle tasks, too; however, compared to other browsers, Dia requires your permission to proceed. While it’s a good control to have, it can get tiring easily, especially if you have used other AI browsers before.

While it was built by The Browser Company, the company behind the Arc browser, it has not brought any of those elements here, but this is easily the cleanest and most minimal browser on this entire list.

Pricing & availability:

  • Free: chat on any tab, create Skills, attach files
  • Pro: $20/month for unlimited chat usage
  • Platforms: macOS

6. Sigma AI Browser – Best for Creators and Content Makers

Sigma turns your browser into a full creative workspace. Alongside AI chat, it includes built-in tools for writing, image generation, video and music creation, and even SEO-friendly content drafting. You can switch between multiple AI models, such as GPT-5.1 and Gemini 2.5, depending on the task — for example, use one model for brainstorming and another for generating visuals.

In practice, it’s great for creators and marketers. You can open a product page, turn its details into an SEO brief, generate matching hero images, and draft a complete blog post, all without ever leaving the browser. Everything stays in one place, from idea to publish-ready content. However, in our experience, the browser has some bugs, such as entire chats disappearing at times or inconsistent-quality results. But for day-to-day use, they are minor and do not get in the way for the most part.

Pricing & availability:

  • Free core usage; advanced features via paid plans
  • Platforms: Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android

7. Fellou AI – Best for Task Automation and Data Scraping

Fellou is built to automate web tasks from start to finish. It can log in to sites, bypass CAPTCHA tests, browse multiple pages, and turn everything it finds into clear, structured reports. With its Eko framework, you can create custom AI agents to handle repetitive work exactly the way you want.

For example, you can tell Fellou to collect competitor prices from 20 different retailers, summarize customer reviews to measure sentiment, or fill out long procurement forms automatically. It’s a browser made for people who need to get data and reports fast, without manual clicks or copy-paste.

Pricing & availability:

  • Freemium: advanced features from $19.9/month (credit‑based)
  • Platforms: Desktop

Final Thoughts

AI browsers are still evolving, and after using several of them, I’d say it’s best to keep your expectations low. They currently handle only simple tasks, such as filling out forms or making purchases. However, they can be useful from time to time and have the potential to automate bigger workflows in the future, such as creating lead funnels or applying for jobs with precise details.

  • Safari vs. Chrome Comparison

title.rendered: WhatsApp for Apple Watch: Everything You Need to Know

content.rendered:
After years of anticipation, WhatsApp has finally arrived on the Apple Watch. The new dedicated Apple Watch app lets you browse chats, send text and voice messages within recent conversations, and even receive new messages and WhatsApp calls right from your wrist. You no longer need to rely on notification mirroring or third-party apps, as the Apple Watch experience is now complete with one of the world’s most popular messaging apps.

Keep reading to learn how to get and use WhatsApp on your Apple Watch.

Table of Contents
  • All the Ways You Can Use WhatsApp on Apple Watch
  • Compatibility and Requirements
  • How to Set Up WhatsApp on Apple Watch
  • How to Use WhatsApp on Apple Watch
  • Chatting Made Simple, Right on Your Wrist…

All the Ways You Can Use WhatsApp on Apple Watch

Like the iPad version, Meta has designed WhatsApp for Apple Watch to work natively. It gives you quick access to all your recent chats without having to reach for your iPhone. That said, the Apple Watch app requires you to open WhatsApp on your iPhone the first time you try to open it on your watch. The interface fits beautifully into the watchOS design, offering a smooth and intuitive experience.

Here’s everything the new app can do:

  • Browse Through Chats: The app syncs all the conversations from your iPhone’s WhatsApp, allowing you to scroll through them right on your wrist. All the chats are available to you in full and not just in notifications. Messages appear in a clean, easy-to-read layout optimized for quick glances.
  • Reply Effortlessly: Use voice dictation, preset replies, emoji reactions, or the dedicated QWERTY keypad to respond to messages directly. This is especially handy for quick responses when you’re on the move.
  • Send Voice Messages: Just like WhatsApp on iPhone, tap the Microphone icon at the bottom-right corner to record and send a voice message instead of a regular text message.
  • Get Call Notifications: Receive incoming WhatsApp call alerts on your Apple Watch and choose to answer or decline them without reaching for your iPhone.
  • Media Viewing: View images shared in your chats directly on your Apple Watch, so you don’t need to open your iPhone to see what’s been sent. For videos, the app shows the [Unsupported, View on iPhone] dialog box.
  • Stay in Sync with Your iPhone: Every action on your watch, such as sent replies, is reflected instantly on your iPhone, maintaining message continuity across devices.

Oddly enough, the app lacks some of the more fun and useful features, such as viewing status updates, making calls, and starting a new chat.

It seems WhatsApp decided to stick to the basics, and honestly, I’m not complaining. We now have a native app that offers a buttery-smooth experience, perfectly aligned with what users have been waiting for.

Compatibility and Requirements

Before trying to install WhatsApp on Apple Watch, make sure you meet these requirements:

  • An Apple Watch Series 4 or newer running watchOS 10 or later
  • An iPhone running iOS 18 or later
  • Latest version of WhatsApp installed on your iPhone

How to Set Up WhatsApp on Apple Watch

Although every app installed on your iPhone automatically appears on your Apple Watch if it’s compatible, you can manually install WhatsApp on your Apple Watch if it doesn’t appear automatically. Here’s how:

  1. Open the App Store app on your Apple Watch.
  2. Here, use the search bar to search for WhatsApp Messenger.
  3. Locate and select the WhatsApp Messenger in the search results.
  4. Tap Install.

Once installed, the app automatically links to your existing WhatsApp account on your iPhone, no additional login required.

How to Use WhatsApp on Apple Watch

Using WhatsApp on Apple Watch is simple. Here’s how:

  1. Open the app to view your recent chats.
  2. Tap any conversation to read or reply, and scroll using the Digital Crown. You can reply with voice dictation, quick responses, or emojis, and even view photos sent to you.
  3. When a WhatsApp call comes in, answer or decline it directly from your wrist.

Chatting Made Simple, Right on Your Wrist…

WhatsApp on Apple Watch delivers exactly what users have been asking for: quick message access, instant replies, and call handling, all from the wrist. And since it took Meta so long to deliver, the app feels well-designed, responsive, and tightly integrated with iOS, making it one of the best smartwatch messaging experiences available today.

Tried WhatsApp on your Apple Watch yet? Share your first impressions in the comments below.

Related Posts:

  • How to Back Up WhatsApp Chat Messages on iPhone
  • How to mirror your Apple Watch to iPhone
  • How to use WhatsApp Communities on iPhone
  • How to Mirror Your Apple Watch on Your iPhone

aioseo_head_json.description: WhatsApp is finally on Apple Watch! Learn how to install, set up, and use WhatsApp on your wrist to send messages, reply with voice, and get calls without needing your iPhone.

itemListElement.name: WhatsApp for Apple Watch: Everything You Need to Know

@graph.name: How to get WhatsApp notifications on your Apple Watch
@graph.description: Enable WhatsApp notifications on your Apple Watch by adjusting notification settings on your iPhone and Watch app.

step.name: Enable WhatsApp notifications on iPhone
step.text: Open the Settings app on your iPhone, tap Notifications, then WhatsApp, and turn on Allow Notifications.

itemListElement.text: Launch Settings on your iPhone.
Tap Notifications and select WhatsApp.
Toggle on Allow Notifications.

step.name: Open the Watch app
step.text: On your paired iPhone, open the Watch app to manage Apple Watch settings.

itemListElement.text: Find and tap the Watch app icon.

step.name: Adjust notification settings in Watch app
step.text: Tap Notifications, scroll down to MIRROR IPHONE ALERTS FROM, and enable the toggle for WhatsApp.

itemListElement.text: Tap Notifications in the Watch app.
Scroll to MIRROR IPHONE ALERTS FROM.
Enable WhatsApp notifications.

@graph.name: How to Install WhatsApp on Apple Watch with WatchChat 2
@graph.description: Install and use WhatsApp on your Apple Watch by setting up the WatchChat 2 app and pairing it with your iPhone.

step.name: Download WatchChat 2 on Apple Watch
step.text: Purchase and download the WatchChat 2 app for $2.99 on your Apple Watch using the paired iPhone's Watch app.

itemListElement.text: Open the Watch app on your paired iPhone.
Go to the App Store → Discover Watch Apps on iPhone.
Tap on the Search tab, type WatchChat 2, and download it.

step.name: Open WatchChat 2 on Apple Watch
step.text: Launch the WatchChat 2 app on your Apple Watch. A QR code will appear the first time you open it.

itemListElement.text: Press the Digital Crown to open your apps.
Tap WatchChat 2 to launch it.
Note the displayed QR code.

step.name: Pair WhatsApp with WatchChat 2
step.text: Open WhatsApp on your iPhone, tap Settings → WhatsApp Web, then scan the QR code displayed on your Apple Watch.

itemListElement.text: Open WhatsApp on your iPhone.
Go to Settings → WhatsApp Web.
Use your iPhone to scan the QR code from your Apple Watch.

step.name: Start using WhatsApp on Apple Watch
step.text: Once scanned, your iPhone and Apple Watch will be connected, and you can now send and receive WhatsApp messages directly from your watch.

itemListElement.text: Wait for the pairing to complete.
Access your chats and start messaging from your Apple Watch.

keyPoints.title: Enable WhatsApp Notifications on iPhone and Mirror to Apple Watch
keyPoints.explanation: Configure notification settings on your iPhone for WhatsApp, then mirror these alerts to your Apple Watch via the Watch app to stay updated on messages.

keyPoints.title: Access WhatsApp on Apple Watch with WatchChat 2
keyPoints.explanation: Download WatchChat 2 and connect it to WhatsApp Web by scanning a QR code, allowing you to send and receive messages directly from your watch.

keyPoints.title: Read and Respond to WhatsApp Messages on Apple Watch
keyPoints.explanation: Use WatchChat 2 to open conversations, scroll through messages, and reply using voice dictation, scribble, or quick reply options from your wrist.

keyPoints.title: Start New WhatsApp Chats from Apple Watch
keyPoints.explanation: Open WatchChat 2, choose contacts, and compose or send new messages via voice or text inputs without needing your phone.

keyPoints.title: View Photos and Videos on WhatsApp Using Apple Watch
keyPoints.explanation: Tap on media within chats in WatchChat 2 to view and download images; video functionality is limited but ongoing improvements are possible.

Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: How to Find Your Parked Car Location on iPhone

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • iPhone connection needed for parked car tracking: Your iPhone must connect to your car via CarPlay or Bluetooth; disconnecting helps Maps automatically record your parked location.
  • Enable ‘Show Parked Location’ in Settings: Go to Settings → Maps and toggle on Show Parked Location to let Apple Maps save your parking spot automatically.
  • How to find your parked car using Apple Maps: Once disconnected, Apple Maps drops a pin at your last car location—just tap it to view details or get walking directions.
  • Feature accuracy and limitations: The parked car marker depends on recent connections and may be less precise indoors, in underground garages, or rural areas.
  • Fix issues or try alternatives: Check that Location Services and Maps permissions are active, or use Google Maps’ parking reminder as a backup option.

We’ve all been in situations where we’ve parked our car in a crowded lot and forgotten where we left it. But be at ease, your iPhone can come to the rescue! With Apple Maps, you can easily track your car’s location and save yourself from the inconvenience. Here, I’ll show you how to use your iPhone to find your parked car location.

Table of Contents
  • Things to Consider Before Getting started
  • How to Enable 'Show Parked Location' on Your iPhone
  • Find Your Parked Car Using Apple Maps on iPhone
    • Limitations of Using Maps' Parked Car Feature
  • What to Do If You Can't Find Your Parked Car Location on Your iPhone?
  • Alternatives to Finding Your Car
  • Wrapping up…

Things to Consider Before Getting started

  • You must pair your iOS device to your car’s CarPlay or Bluetooth system. Whenever your iPhone gets disconnected from your car’s Bluetooth or CarPlay system, it drops a parked car marker in the Maps app. For example, when you exit your vehicle, it severs the connection between the two.
  • Most newer cars have CarPlay. To check support for your vehicle, visit Apple’s CarPlay page. If you can’t see your car on the list, you can still use the car’s Bluetooth system.
  • Ensure Location Services, Significant Locations, and Bluetooth are enabled on your iPhone.
  • If you’re using a data connection, be sure to enable Cellular data for Maps.
    To do this, head to Settings → Cellular → Show All → Toggle Maps on.

How to Enable ‘Show Parked Location’ on Your iPhone

  1. Go to Settings on your iPhone, tap Apps, and select Maps.
  2. Under the Your Car section, toggle Show Parked Location on.

With this turned on, you should be able to see a Parked Car marker for your car’s current location.

Also, if you ever change your mind and find the feature annoying, you can just toggle off Show Parked Location to stop showing your parked location on your iPhone.

Find Your Parked Car Using Apple Maps on iPhone

With the feature turned on, Maps will automatically drop a marker on Maps when you disconnect your iPhone from your car. 

You should see a notification indicating that Maps dropped a pin to mark your parking location. If you don’t see a notification, you probably didn’t connect to your vehicle’s CarPlay or Bluetooth system. Also, go to Settings → Notifications → Maps and ensure Time Sensitive Notifications is enabled.

To use it, just choose Parked Car below Siri Suggestions on the search card. Alternatively, type “parked car” in the search field. This should display your car’s location. If these don’t work, you can check via Maps. To do this:

  1. Open the Maps app on your iPhone.
  2. You’ll see a blue Parked Car marker on where you parked your car.
  3. Tap the pin to see more details about the location.
  4. Select Directions to get navigations to your parked car.

Tap the three-dot icon to get more options. You can add a note to help you remember the parking location, or Add a Photo to help you remember the place visually.

Limitations of Using Maps’ Parked Car Feature

  • Your car’s location will be based on the most recent time it was connected to your iPhone. So, suppose you last connected with your vehicle from location A but moved it to location B without connecting your iPhone to your car. Your car’s location will still be in location A.
  • When you park your car at a familiar location, such as your workplace or home, it won’t be marked.
  • Using this feature can also be confusing if you park inside establishments. While it will show the location, it can’t pinpoint the exact spot and level you’re on, so it’s wise to take note or take a photo of your exact parking slot.
  • While it works well in metropolitan areas, some users note problems using the feature in rural areas.

What to Do If You Can’t Find Your Parked Car Location on Your iPhone?

If you have already paired your iPhone to CarPlay or Bluetooth but still can’t see your parked car in Maps, check your settings:

  1. Go to Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services → toggle it on.
  2. Head back to Location Services → System Services → Significant Locations & Routes. Now, authenticate your Face ID and toggle it on.

Alternatives to Finding Your Car

If you aren’t a fan of Maps and prefer using Google Maps, you can also use Google Maps to save the location where you parked.

To do this,

  1. Park your car.
  2. Open Google Maps, tap the blue pin (where you’re currently located), and select Save Parking.
  3. When heading back to the parking lot, tap the P pin, then choose Start. This will give you directions on how to get back to your car.

Wrapping up…

Forgetting where you parked your car can be a headache. Thankfully, you can use Apple Maps on your iPhone to find your parked car’s location.

What do you think about this feature? Do you use it or prefer other methods to locate your car? Let us know in the comments section!

Read more:

  • How to use Apple Maps offline on iPhone
  • Best GPS navigation apps for iPhone

aioseo_meta_data.description: With Apple Maps, you can easily track your car’s location when parked in a crowded area. Here’s how to find the location of your car on your iPhone.

focus.keyphrase: Find Your Parked Car Location on iPhone

keyPoints.title: Car Connection Requirements
keyPoints.explanation: Your iPhone needs to be paired with your car’s CarPlay or Bluetooth system, as disconnecting drops the parked car marker in Maps.

keyPoints.title: Enable 'Show Parked Location' Feature
keyPoints.explanation: Navigate to Settings > Maps and toggle on 'Show Parked Location' to automatically mark where you parked.

keyPoints.title: Finding Your Parked Car with Apple Maps
keyPoints.explanation: After disconnecting from your vehicle, your iPhone drops a pin in Maps; you can view and navigate to this location for easy retrieval.

keyPoints.title: Limitations of the Parked Car Feature
keyPoints.explanation: The feature relies on recent connections and may not pinpoint the exact spot inside establishments or in rural areas.

keyPoints.title: Troubleshooting and Alternatives
keyPoints.explanation: If your car isn't showing, check location settings, or use Google Maps for parking location and directions.

title.rendered: Here’s Everything New in iOS 26.2 Beta 1

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Lock Screen Customization Upgrade: iOS 26.2 adds a Liquid Glass slider so you can adjust the clock’s transparency or make it completely opaque for better visibility.
  • Enhanced Sleep Score System: The updated sleep tracking in iOS 26.2 and watchOS 26.2 now scores rest quality based on how refreshed you feel, ranging from Very Low to Very High.
  • Password Management Improvements: A new ‘Excluded Websites’ option in the Passwords app lets you disable auto-fill for specific sites, improving login control and privacy.
  • AirPods Live Translation in the EU: AirPods now support real-time translation across English, French, German, and Spanish, finally expanding Live Translation to European users.
  • New Features in Freeform and Reminders: Freeform adds Table support for structured planning, while Reminders introduces an ‘Urgent’ toggle to trigger alarms for time-sensitive tasks.

iOS 26.2 just rolled out, but Apple has already moved on to testing iOS 26.2. The developer beta of iOS 26.2 introduces fresh ways to customize, enhanced health tracking, and tweaks to several apps. Let’s dive into what’s new with iOS 26.2 beta 1.

Lock Screen Customization

A new Liquid Glass slider lets you fine-tune the clock’s frosted or clear appearance on the lock screen. You can adjust the clock’s transparency or switch to a fully opaque look.

Updated Sleep Score

iOS 26.2, alongside watchOS 26.2, revamps the Sleep Score system to more accurately mirror users’ post-sleep feelings:

  • Very Low: 0–40
  • Low: 41–60
  • OK: 61–80
  • High: 81–95
  • Very High: 96–100

Password Management

A new “Excluded Websites” option in the Passwords app lets users manage sites where saved credentials are disabled.

AirPods Live Translation Arrives in the EU

Following iOS 26.1’s language expansion, Live Translation for AirPods has finally landed in the European Union in iOS 26.2. The rollout was stalled to comply with EU Digital Markets Act regulations. This feature, supported on AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2, and AirPods 4 with ANC, now includes multiple languages like English, French, German, and Spanish.

Freeform Gets Tables

The Freeform app now supports Tables, making collaborative boards more structured and versatile.

Reminders with Alarms

The Reminder app has new “Urgent” toggle that adds an alarm when a reminder is due. When the reminder alarm goes off, you’ll see snooze options, countdowns, and distinct blue alerts right on the Lock Screen.

Podcasts Improvements

Podcasts now include auto-generated chapters, cross-podcast mentions, and quick access to links mentioned in transcripts.

AirDrop Expansion (Upcoming)

Although the feature isn’t live in this update, references in iOS 26.2 hint at an upcoming AirDrop PIN-sharing feature that could extend AirDrop access for non-contacts up to 30 days, up from the current 10-minute limit.

Weather and News Enhancements

The Weather app now includes relative time alerts like “next Tuesday.” Meanwhile, Apple News introduces redesigned navigation with quick-access category buttons and a dedicated Following tab.

Flash for Alerts

The Flash for Alerts option in Accessibility now lets the screen flash when notifications arrive. Previously, this setting used only the rear LED on the iPhone. You can choose to use only the screen flash or both the screen and LED flashes together.

Safety Alerts

Enhanced Safety Alerts now allow users to handle earthquake and threat notifications with better reliability.

Availability and Compatibility

The iOS 26.2 developer beta is open for registered developers, with the public beta anticipated later this week. A stable release is expected to drop between December 9 and December 16. Compatibility extends to all iPhones that support iOS 26.

Do these new features pique your interest? We’d love to hear your take in the comments below.

excerpt.rendered: Apple is testing iOS 26.2 with exciting upgrades, including a Liquid Glass clock for the Lock Screen, improved Sleep tracking, and AirPods Live Translation across the EU.

keyPoints.title: Lock Screen Customization Upgrade
keyPoints.explanation: iOS 26.2 introduces a Liquid Glass slider, allowing users to fine-tune the lock screen clock's transparency or switch it to fully opaque.

keyPoints.title: Enhanced Sleep Score System
keyPoints.explanation: The new sleep score system in iOS 26.2 and watchOS 26.2 offers more accurate reflections of users' post-sleep feelings, with categories from Very Low to Very High.

keyPoints.title: Password Management Improvements
keyPoints.explanation: A new 'Excluded Websites' option in the Passwords app helps users manage sites where saved credentials are disabled.

keyPoints.title: AirPods Live Translation in the EU
keyPoints.explanation: Live Translation for AirPods has finally arrived in the European Union on supported models, enabling real-time multi-language translation, including English, French, German, and Spanish.

keyPoints.title: New Features in Freeform and Reminders Apps
keyPoints.explanation: Freeform now supports Tables for better structured collaboration, while Reminders gets an 'Urgent' toggle that adds alarms and notifications for due reminders.

title.rendered: iPhone 18 Pro May Feature One New Color Option

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple may drop black from iPhone 18 Pro palette as it tests burgundy, brown, and purple for a single new Pro-exclusive color.
  • Burgundy would mark a red-toned first for Pro models, standing apart from standard iPhones’ bright (PRODUCT)RED finishes.
  • Brown would be an entirely new shade for Apple, while purple could echo iPhone 14 Pro’s Deep Purple with a slight update.
  • Color shake-up continues Apple’s trend toward bold tones, following iPhone 17 Pro’s Silver, Cosmic Orange, and Deep Blue lineup.
  • Leaks come from a mixed-reliability source, so these iPhone 18 Pro color options remain speculative with plenty of time for changes.

Apple is reportedly in the midst of deciding on a new color palette for its upcoming iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, but only one final shade may come into play. This speculation originates from Instant Digital, a prominent leaker on Weibo with a mixed but noteworthy record when it comes to Apple predictions.

Apple Reportedly Testing Burgundy, Brown, and Purple

The latest leak suggests Apple is trying out three potential hues: burgundy, brown, and purple. These shades would be reserved for the Pro and Pro Max models of the iPhone 18 series, anticipated to debut in September 2026. However, the leaker later noted that just one of these colors is expected to go into production. While specific details on the exact tones are scarce, concept images on social media offer a glimpse of the possibilities. A burgundy choice would introduce a red-toned option to the Pro lineup for the first time, differing from the bright (PRODUCT)RED seen on standard models. The brown option, should it be selected, would be entirely new territory for Apple. As for purple, it would echo the Deep Purple of the iPhone 14 Pro, albeit with a possible twist.

No Black Model This Time?

Along with these potential new finishes, there’s a suggestion that Apple may forego a black option altogether for the iPhone 18 Pro series. This aligns with the design choices of the iPhone 17 Pro lineup, which came in Silver, Cosmic Orange, and Deep Blue, favoring bold, jewel-toned colors over traditional ones like graphite or space black. Apple has been shifting towards these more vibrant metallic hues for its Pro models, signifying a trend that might continue with the iPhone 18 Pro, should one of these darker new shades take center stage in place of black.

Track Record of the Leaker

Instant Digital has previously provided accurate information regarding Apple products, such as the Yellow iPhone 14, the frosted back glass of the iPhone 15, and the Titanium Milanese Loop for the Apple Watch Ultra 2. Nonetheless, not all leaks have hit the mark, so it’s wise to consider this color rumor plausible yet unverified. Given the lengthy lead time before Apple’s next Pro models hit shelves, the company’s design decisions could still pivot. Nevertheless, this early insight into potential color offerings suggests Apple is maintaining its trajectory toward luxury-oriented finishes for its premium smartphones.

Would Apple’s potential color overhaul catch your interest? Share your thoughts below.

title.rendered: WhatsApp Arrives on Apple Watch: Key Details

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • WhatsApp now fully supports Apple Watch with a dedicated app that offers messaging, emoji reactions, voice notes, and media previews without using your iPhone.
  • Full chat access replaces limited notifications, letting you scroll entire conversations, send messages, and view stickers and images directly on the watch.
  • Call alerts and chat history are now visible, giving you real-time caller ID and a more complete record of past messages than the old mirrored alerts.
  • Works on Apple Watch Series 4 or newer running watchOS 10+, but still requires your iPhone nearby for syncing and connectivity.
  • Watch out for cellular model limitations — the app isn’t fully standalone yet, so remote use without your iPhone isn’t supported (but may come later).

Meta’s WhatsApp has officially arrived on Apple Watch, marking the end of its previously limited capabilities on the wearable. The fully-featured app is now available to download by all users following a brief beta period through TestFlight.

A Full Chat Experience on Apple Watch

Apple Watch users were previously restricted to reading and replying to notifications mirrored from their iPhones. This new official app changes that. In a report by Engadget, Meta notes that the app introduces a host of sought-after features, providing a more comprehensive chatting experience directly from the watch.

Users can now scroll through entire conversations, including long ones, without needing their iPhones. The app enables sending written messages, recording and sending voice notes, reacting with emojis, and viewing images and stickers more clearly on the watch.

Call Notifications and Chat History

Besides messaging, call notifications are now accessible, indicating who’s calling, which lets users decide swiftly whether to pick up their phone. The app also offers an extended view of chat history, overcoming limitations of earlier mirrored notifications.

Meta reassures that end-to-end encryption remains active for all communications through the Apple Watch app, maintaining user privacy and security.

Compatibility and Installation

Per TechRadar, the new WhatsApp app works with Apple Watch Series 4 and newer running watchOS 10 or later. Users need their iPhone nearby with the latest version of WhatsApp for proper syncing and connection.

To get the app, users can search WhatsApp in the App Store directly from their Apple Watch, or use the Watch app on their iPhone, navigate to the My Watch tab, find WhatsApp, and proceed with installation.

Why It Matters

The launch signifies a significant advancement for WhatsApp’s utility on wearables. Although messaging apps like Telegram and Messenger already offered dedicated Apple Watch apps, WhatsApp was lagging for years. Now, Apple Watch users can finally enjoy similar interactions and convenience that Android smartwatch users have had.

Meta has hinted that additional features are on the horizon, potentially introducing standalone app support for cellular Apple Watch models, which would enhance WhatsApp’s usability on the go.

How do you feel about this new WhatsApp feature on the Apple Watch? Share your thoughts below.

excerpt.rendered: WhatsApp finally arrives on Apple Watch with full chat access, voice notes, emoji reactions, and media previews, bringing true messaging freedom to your wrist.

title.rendered: What’s New in the Phone App with iOS 26

content.rendered:
The humble Phone app that almost never gets any new features, finally got the complete redesign it deserves in iOS 26. And from a usage perspective, we really like everything about the new Liquid Glass design style, the useful AI features that handle spam calls, etc. In the article, we will dive into all the features Apple introduced in iOS 26, so you can take advantage of all of these new features.

Table of Contents
  • 1. A Fresh Unified Design
  • 2. Pin Your Favorites
  • 3. Call Screening Takes Over Unknown Calls
  • 4. Hold Assist Waits So You Don’t Have To
  • 5. AI-Powered Live Translation and Voicemail Summaries
  • 6. Call Filtering for Unknown Numbers
  • 7. SharePlay Over Phone Calls
  • 8. Personalized Monograms and Contact Posters
  • 9. Better Call Quality
  • Bonus: New Ringtones and Cross-Device Support
  • Final Thoughts

1. A Fresh Unified Design

The first thing you’ll notice is the new unified layout. Apple has merged the Recents, Favorites, and Voicemail tabs into one single screen called Calls. It’s cleaner, more organized, and fits right in with the new Liquid Glass aesthetic that gives iOS 26 its translucent, glossy finish. Your favorite contacts appear at the top, followed by your recent calls, voicemails, and missed numbers, all in one scrollable view.

The bottom navigation bar is simplified too, now showing only Calls, Contacts, Keypad, and Search. A small three-line icon at the top-right corner replaces extra tabs, giving you quick access to voicemail and other settings.

If you’re not a fan of change, Apple’s got you covered. You can switch back to the old tabbed interface any time by tapping the menu icon and selecting Classic view. The Phone app will immediately revert to the familiar iOS 18-style layout,  and yes, you can switch back again whenever you want.

2. Pin Your Favorites

You can now pin your most important contacts at the top of the unified Calls tab. Simply tap Edit > Edit Favorites, then add numbers, FaceTime contacts, or even message shortcuts. There’s no strict limit on how many you can pin, though more than six will be hidden behind a Show All button.

3. Call Screening Takes Over Unknown Calls

One of the most practical additions is Call Screening. When you get a call from an unknown number, your iPhone can now pick it up for you, ask who’s calling, and display their response live on your screen. You can then decide whether to answer or ignore it; no more awkward spam calls break your focus.

It’s available in multiple languages and regions, including English (US, UK, India, Australia), French, German, Spanish, Japanese, Mandarin, and more. You can enable the feature from Settings > Apps > Phone and set Screen Unknown Callers to Ask Reason for Calling or directly to Silence.

4. Hold Assist Waits So You Don’t Have To

We’ve all been there, stuck on hold with customer support for what feels like forever. Hold Assist finally fixes that. When a call puts you on hold, your iPhone will stay on the line for you and alert you the moment a human picks up. You can keep scrolling, working, or relaxing while your iPhone listens for your turn.

This feature is rolling out in several regions, including the US, UK, Canada, India, Germany, and Japan. It’s enabled by default, and you can change it in the Settings app > Apps > Phone and enable Hold Assist Detection.

5. AI-Powered Live Translation and Voicemail Summaries

With Apple Intelligence in iOS 26, the Phone app is getting smarter. Live Translation lets you talk to people who speak different languages, translating your voice and theirs in real time. It’s powered by on-device AI for privacy and works across calls and FaceTime.

Meanwhile, your voicemails now come with short AI-generated summaries, giving you a quick idea of what the message is about without having to play it.

6. Call Filtering for Unknown Numbers

If you’d rather not even see unknown numbers, iOS 26 lets you filter them out automatically. Turn on Call Filtering in Settings > Apps > Phone, and your iPhone will quietly move unknown numbers into a separate Unknown Callers list under the More menu in the Phone app.

7. SharePlay Over Phone Calls

Apple has extended SharePlay to regular phone calls, letting you do much more than just talk. While chatting, you can now share your screen to guide someone through settings, listen to music together via Apple Music, or even watch movies in sync through supported streaming apps, all without switching to FaceTime.

It uses the same smooth SharePlay interface you’ve seen before, and everything stays synced in real time. The feature works on both Wi-Fi and cellular, and participants can control playback individually while remaining connected on the call.

8. Personalized Monograms and Contact Posters

The new Monogram styles make it easy to personalize your Contact Poster without overcomplicating things. You can pick from a few clean designs, change colors or fonts, and preview your changes before saving. Edits sync through iCloud, so your chosen look appears on all your Apple devices and when you call others. It’s a small touch that makes calls feel more personal while keeping the interface simple and elegant.

9. Better Call Quality

Voice clarity gets a real upgrade in iOS 26 thanks to high-quality cellular calling. Apple has optimized how your iPhone handles audio over both 4G and 5G networks, using enhanced codecs and better noise isolation. This means crisper, more natural voices and fewer distortions, even when the signal isn’t perfect. The improvement is especially noticeable on older or narrowband connections, giving them near-HD quality.

It’s supported on iPhone 16e and later, and users will notice clearer calls in busy areas, during weak network coverage, or when switching between Wi-Fi and cellular.

Bonus: New Ringtones and Cross-Device Support

Apple has also added seven new ringtones, including Little Bird, alongside alternate versions of the popular Reflections tone. You’ll find them under Settings > Sounds & Haptics.

Final Thoughts

I have always been divided between Pixels and iPhones. With iOS 26, Apple finally gave most of the features, especially in the phone app, that made Pixel phones exciting to me. Most spam cannot reach me; my iPhone stays on hold for me, and I can contact anyone who does not speak the language I know. These are features that actually make sense to have when you need them. 

Read More:

  • How to Switch Back to the Classic Phone App Layout

keyPoints.title: A Fresh Unified Design
keyPoints.explanation: The iPhone Phone app now has a clean, unified layout combining Recents, Favorites, and Voicemail into one sleek, Liquid Glass styled interface, with easy toggle options for classic view.

keyPoints.title: Pin Your Favorites
keyPoints.explanation: Users can pin important contacts at the top of the Calls tab, making it easier to access frequent contacts, with no strict limit on pins.

keyPoints.title: Call Screening for Unknown Calls
keyPoints.explanation: AI-powered call screening allows the iPhone to answer and ask unknown callers who they are, helping users avoid spam and unwanted calls.

keyPoints.title: Hold Assist for On-Hold Calls
keyPoints.explanation: Hold Assist keeps you on hold while your iPhone listens in and notifies you when a live person answers, so you can relax or continue other tasks.

keyPoints.title: AI Live Translation and Voicemail Summaries
keyPoints.explanation: Real-time language translation during calls and AI-generated voicemail summaries help users communicate across languages and quickly understand messages.

Key Takeaways:

  • How shared photos work in iMessage: Photos exchanged through iMessage are stored in each chat’s Photos section, letting you easily view all shared media in one place.
  • Enable ‘Shared with You’ for seamless access: Turn on Shared with You in Settings → Messages to automatically view shared images in the Photos app, with controls for each contact.
  • Where to find shared iMessage photos: Open chat details to see the Photos section, or go to the Photos app → Shared with You album to browse all shared images together.
  • Fix missing shared photos on iPhone: If photos don’t appear, ensure Shared with You is enabled, indexing is complete, and iOS is updated to the latest version.
  • Keep shared media organized: Save key images right away, clear outdated ones in chat details, and use Photos app filters to search and manage shared pictures efficiently.

Looking for that vacation photo your friend sent you on iMessage, but couldn’t find it? Don’t worry, your iPhone keeps them organized in one place, so you don’t need to scroll through hundreds of messages.

In this guide, you’ll learn the easiest ways to view all the photos shared with you in iMessage, whether you want to see them in a chat or access them from your phone’s library. Let’s get started.

Table of Contents
  • What Are Shared Photos in iMessage?
  • Step 1: Set Up the Shared with You Feature for iMessage
    • Enable Automatic Sync for All Shared Photos
    • Control Sharing for Individual Contacts
  • Step 2: View iMessage Shared Photos on iPhone
    • Via iMessage
    • Access Shared Photos in the Photos App
  • Can’t See Shared Photos? Check These Settings
  • Quick Tips for Managing Shared Photos
  • Revisit Memories in iMessage!

What Are Shared Photos in iMessage?

Whenever someone sends or receives a photo through the Messages app (a.k.a. iMessage), Apple automatically keeps a record of those images in that chat’s Photos section.

In iOS 26, Apple has refined this layout, making it faster and cleaner. You can now open a chat, tap a contact’s name, and see every image exchanged in one place. 

You can also access these images directly in the Photos app under the Shared with You section. So even if you forget who sent what, iOS has you covered.

Step 1: Set Up the Shared with You Feature for iMessage

The Shared with You feature automatically collects photos your contacts send through iMessage and displays them inside your iPhone’s Photos app.

Enable Automatic Sync for All Shared Photos

  1. Open the Settings app → Tap Apps at the bottom → Choose Messages.
  2. Scroll down to and tap Shared with You.
  3. In the app list below, toggle on Photos as well as any others you’d like.

Important:

  • If you delete a conversation in Messages, any photos and videos from that thread are also deleted from the Shared with You section. 
  • To keep them permanently, save them to your Library before deleting the chat.

Control Sharing for Individual Contacts

You can choose whose photos and videos are allowed to appear in the Share with You section automatically. It allows you to avoid cluttering your gallery with unnecessary memes and images.

  1. Open the Messages app → Select a conversation with your contact. 
  2. Tap your contact’s name at the top to display their details. 
  3. Scroll down a bit and toggle on Show in Shared with You to make sure you see that contact’s shared pictures in the Photos app.
  4. Tap the left arrow at the top to exit the contact details and return to the conversation in Messages.

Step 2: View iMessage Shared Photos on iPhone

You can check the shared photos collection for a dedicated contact or all in a single album. Here’s how to do both:

Via iMessage

  1. Launch the Messages app on your iPhone and open the conversation that includes the photo(s) you want to revisit. 
  2. Tap the contact’s name (or the group chat title) at the top. This opens the chat details screen. 
  3. Move to the Photos section. Here you will see all the photos exchanged in the thread.  
  4. Now, tap any photo to view it in full screen. Else, tap and hold it to save, copy, share, or delete it.

Pro Tip: From the context menu, select Show in Conversation to jump back to the original message where the photo was sent.

Access Shared Photos in the Photos App 

If you’d rather browse all shared iMessage photos in one place, you can also do it directly in the Photos app. 

  1. Open the Photos app and ensure you are in the Library view. 
  2. Tap the three-dot icon at the top. 
  3. Select Filter from the dropdown and tap Shared with You.

It will show all the photos and videos people have sent you via Messages. Now, you can edit the photo or video, create a slideshow, make a Live Sticker, and much more.

Can’t See Shared Photos? Check These Settings 

If your shared photos aren’t appearing, don’t panic. It’s often just a setting or sync issue. 

  • Ensure Shared with You feature is enabled in Settings and individual chats.  
  • In Photos, tap the three-dot icon → View Options and select Shared with You. So, it will appear under Filter. 
  • After updating to iOS 26, your phone might take a bit to re-index all your messages and attachments. Keep your iPhone connected to Wi-Fi and plugged in. It’ll sort itself out in the background.

Quick Tips for Managing Shared Photos 

We all exchange a lot of media on iMessage every day, so the Shared with You section quickly gets cluttered. 

  • Save what matters: When someone sends an important photo or video, save it immediately. 
  • Clean up easily: Use the Photos section in chat details to bulk-delete old media from large group chats. 
  • Organize smartly: Mark favorite photos or videos directly in the Photos app for long-term storage. 
  • Smart search filter: Try searching for a person’s name and a keyword (like “Tom beach”) in the search bar, then go to the Photos section.

Revisit Memories in iMessage! 

Finding shared photos in iMessage used to mean endless scrolling, but not anymore. With iOS 26, Apple’s made it simple to browse every photo shared in a chat, all in one tidy gallery view. So, your shared memories are just a few taps away. 

Have you tried the new iMessage features in iOS 26? Let me know in the comments below!

FAQs

How to search in iMessage?

When you want to find something specific in the Messages app, you can perform a search. On the main All Messages screen, swipe down slightly to display the Search box at the top. Pop in your search term and you’ll see results from every conversation related to that term, including text, photos, links, or other items.

Do iMessage photos get saved?

Even with the Automatic Sharing feature enabled, as explained here, photos and videos you receive in Messages are not saved by default. If you delete the conversation, the photos will be deleted too. You can check out our how-to for saving photos from Messages to your iPhone or iPad to hold onto those important pictures.

Pop in your search term and you’ll see results from every conversation related to that term, including text, photos, links, or other items.

blockGraphs.question: Do iMessage photos get saved?
blockGraphs.answer: Even with the Automatic Sharing feature enabled, as explained here, photos and videos you receive in Messages are not saved by default. If you delete the conversation, the photos will be deleted too. You can check out our how-to for saving photos from Messages to your iPhone or iPad to hold onto those important pictures.

keyPoints.title: Shared Photos in iMessage
keyPoints.explanation: Photos sent and received through iMessage are automatically saved in the chat's Photos section, making it simple to view all exchanged images.

keyPoints.title: Enabling 'Shared with You' Feature
keyPoints.explanation: Activate the 'Shared with You' setting in Settings > Messages to seamlessly collect shared photos in your Photos app and customize sharing options per contact.

keyPoints.title: .accessing Shared Photos on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: View shared images directly within the iMessage chat details under Photos, or see all shared photos in the 'Shared with You' album in the Photos app.

keyPoints.title: Troubleshooting Shared Photos Visibility
keyPoints.explanation: If shared photos aren’t showing up, ensure 'Shared with You' is enabled in Settings and chats, and that your device has indexed the latest iOS updates.

keyPoints.title: Tips for Managing Shared Photos
keyPoints.explanation: Save key shared images immediately, delete old media from chat details, and use search filters in Photos to organize and revisit moments easily.

title.rendered: 15 Aesthetic Thanksgiving Wallpapers for iPhone

content.rendered:
Thanksgiving is just around the corner, making it the perfect time to get festive and give your iPhone a cozy new look! If you’re searching for the perfect Thanksgiving wallpaper, you’ve come to the right place. We’ve rounded up some of the best Thanksgiving wallpapers for iPhone.

From classic autumn vibes to stylish, modern looks, there’s something for everyone to bring a touch of holiday cheer to your iPhone screen. Let the Thanksgiving decorations begin—enjoy the season!

Table of Contents
  • Best 4K Thanksgiving Wallpapers for iPhone
    • Thanksgiving Pumpkin carving wallpaper
    • Stacked Pumpkins wallpaper
    • Cute Turkey Thanksgiving themed wallpaper
    • Fall season Thanksgiving aesthetic wallpaper
    • Classic American Thanksgiving dinner wallpaper
    • Wreath of Leaves Thanksgiving wallpaper
    • Corn maze Thanksgiving wallpaper
    • Pumpkin patch wallpaper
    • Vintage Thanksgiving wallpaper
    • Rustic Thanksgiving wallpaper
    • Classic cornucopia Thanksgiving wallpaper
    • Preppy Thanksgiving wallpaper
    • Thanksgiving thankful wallpaper
    • Stitch Thanksgiving wallpaper
    • Snoopy and Charlie Brown Thanksgiving wallpaper
  • Happy Thanksgiving!

Best 4K Thanksgiving Wallpapers for iPhone

Get into the festive spirit with our handpicked collection of cute and stunning Thanksgiving wallpapers.

1. Thanksgiving Pumpkin Carving

Capture the essence of fall harvest and festive joy with this intricately carved pumpkin on your iPhone screen. Tap the download button to embrace the warmth of this beautiful season.

Download

2. Stacked Pumpkins

This visual feast will surely please your eyes and uplift your festive spirit whenever you unlock your iPhone. Add a touch of charm to your phone’s appearance with this delightful Thanksgiving wallpaper.

Download

3. Cute Turkey Theme

Gobble up the cuteness of Turkey with this beautifully designed wallpaper. It will surely bring a smile to your face and set a warm mood for the holidays. Tap the download button now!

Download

4. Fall Thanksgiving Aesthetic

Embrace the aesthetic beauty of rich, warm hues and delicate autumn leaves, curating a visually pleasing and calming atmosphere on your iPhone. Tap the download button to enchant your iPhone screen.

Download

5. Classic Thanksgiving Dinner

Here’s a glimpse of a traditional Thanksgiving table set with delicious Apple Pie. Mouthwatering right? Evoke a sense of togetherness and gratitude by downloading this wallpaper.

Download

6. Leaf Wreath for Thanksgiving

Looking for a dark iPhone wallpaper to celebrate Thanksgiving? Download this simple wallpaper with a lush green wreath of leaves encircled by “Happy Thanksgiving” wishes. It brings a sense of gratitude without overwhelming colors or patterns.

Download

7. Corn Maze Adventure

Visiting a corn maze on Thanksgiving has become mandatory. To get the same fall essence, download this beautiful corn maze wallpaper for your iPhone. It shows a golden cornfield at sunset, creating a cozy and rustic ambiance.

Download

8. Pumpkin Patch

Get into the autumn spirit with this vibrant pumpkin patch iPhone wallpaper! It brings the beauty of fall harvest and Thanksgiving right to your iPhone screen. Tap the download button and enjoy the charm of the countryside every time you look at your phone.

Download

9. Vintage Thanksgiving

If you love antique designs, this vintage-inspired Thanksgiving wallpaper is perfect for your iPhone. The delicate design features classic fall elements, like rustic orange pumpkins, earthy pinecones, and golden brown leaves.

Download

10. Rustic Thanksgiving

Celebrate Thanksgiving in style with this rustic iPhone wallpaper. Featuring an earthy background adorned with autumn leaves, pumpkins, and acorns, the design offers a countryside vibe. Download the wallpaper now to get the cozy essence of fall.

Download

11. Classic Cornucopia

Thanksgiving is all about having fun harvesting. This elegant Thanksgiving wallpaper showcases a classic cornucopia overflowing with autumn’s harvest, like pumpkins, apples, grapes, and corn. Tap the download button and let this wallpaper remind you of the generosity of Thanksgiving.

Download

12. Preppy Thanksgiving

This vibrant preppy Thanksgiving wallpaper brings all the warmth and coziness of fall to your iPhone screen. The minimal design includes beautiful hand-drawn pumpkins, acorns, pinecones, and golden autumn leaves, perfect for setting a festive mood.

Download

13. “Thankful” Lettering

Thanksgiving is incomplete without potluck and family dinners. This heartwarming Thanksgiving wallpaper brings the spirit of togetherness with a bountiful feast. Download the wallpaper to embrace the appreciation for family, friends, and life’s blessings.

Download

14. Stitch’s Thanksgiving

This playful wallpaper brings a tropical twist to your screen with Stitch enjoying the holiday season. Set against a dark background, the colors pop, creating a fun and relaxed vibe, perfect for any Stitch fan.

Download

15. Snoopy & Charlie Brown Thanksgiving

If you are a classic cartoon fan, download this Thanksgiving wallpaper featuring the iconic Peanuts characters Charlie Brown and Snoopy. Enjoy Thanksgiving with fun in Snoopy style!

Download

Happy Thanksgiving!

As you navigate through the digital landscape of your iPhone, let the Thanksgiving spirit accompany you with every swipe and tap. These wallpapers not only add a festive touch to your device but also serve as a daily reminder of the blessings that surround you. So, as you gather with loved ones and indulge in the season’s delights, carry a piece of Thanksgiving with you wherever you go.

Thank you for reading. Please take a moment to share your favorite design in the comment section below.

mainEntity.name: How to search in iMessage?

acceptedAnswer.text: When you want to find something specific in the Messages app, you can perform a search. On the main All Messages screen, swipe down slightly to display the Search box at the top. Pop in your search term and you’ll see results from every conversation related to that term, including text, photos, links, or other items.

mainEntity.name: Do iMessage photos get saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Even with the Automatic Sharing feature enabled, as explained here, photos and videos you receive in Messages are not saved by default. If you delete the conversation, the photos will be deleted too. You can check out our how-to for saving photos from Messages to your iPhone or iPad to hold onto those important pictures.

mainEntity.name: How to search in iMessage?

acceptedAnswer.text: When you want to find something specific in the Messages app, you can perform a search. On the main All Messages screen, swipe down slightly to display the Search box at the top. Pop in your search term and you’ll see results from every conversation related to that term, including text, photos, links, or other items.

mainEntity.name: Do iMessage photos get saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Even with the Automatic Sharing feature enabled, as explained here, photos and videos you receive in Messages are not saved by default. If you delete the conversation, the photos will be deleted too. You can check out our how-to for saving photos from Messages to your iPhone or iPad to hold onto those important pictures.
